CSEC_BS.name: Computer Science and Economics, B.S.
CSEC_BS.description: Interdepartmental B.S. degree at Yale that integrates computer science and economics.

requirements.name: Discrete Math
requirements.description: Sufficient background in discrete mathematics, e.g., CPSC 2020 or MATH 2440, or AP/IB credit.

requirements.name: Calculus
requirements.description: Sufficient background in calculus, e.g., MATH 1120, or AP/IB credit.

requirements.name: Microeconomics
requirements.description: Sufficient background in microeconomics, e.g., ECON 1110 or ECON 1115, or AP/IB credit.

requirements.name: Macroeconomics
requirements.description: Sufficient background in macroeconomics, e.g., ECON 1111 or ECON 1116, or AP/IB credit.

requirements.name: Introduction to Computer Science
requirements.description: Required core CS course for all CSEC majors.

requirements.name: Data Structures and Programming Techniques
requirements.description: Required core CS course.

requirements.name: Systems Programming and Computer Organization
requirements.description: CPSC 3230. With permission of the DUS and your academic adviser, a more advanced course in the same area may be substituted, in which case it counts here and not as one of the five electives.

requirements.name: Algorithms
requirements.description: CPSC 3650 or CPSC 3660. Only one of the two may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Intermediate Microeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 2121 or ECON 2125.

requirements.name: Econometrics Sequence
requirements.description: One complete two-course econometrics sequence: ECON 1117 with ECON 2123, or ECON 2135 with ECON 2136. S&DS 2410 and S&DS 2420 together may be taken instead of ECON 2135. Both courses must come from the same sequence, so pick a route before you start.

requirements.name: Game Theory
requirements.description: ECON 3351 or CPSC 4550. If you use CPSC 4550 here it cannot also count as the course in the intersection of computer science and economics.

requirements.name: Intersection of CS and Econ
requirements.description: One course in the intersection of computer science and economics, for example CPSC 4550, CPSC 4740, or ECON 4433. Other courses carrying the CSEC intersection attribute also count. This course may not double count as one of the five electives or as the game theory requirement, and it may not be taken outside Yale.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Five electives from Computer Science, Economics, or both. At least two must be in Computer Science and at least one in Economics. ECON 2122, ECON 2259 and S&DS 3650 count. With adviser approval, the fourth and fifth may come from a related department.

requirements.name: Senior Project
requirements.description: Senior requirement: CSEC 4910, a one-term independent project combining computer science and economics. The proposal must be signed by the DUS by the end of the third week of term.

PSYC_BA.name: Psychology, B.A.
PSYC_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology. Broad foundation in mind, brain, and behavior.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: Introduction to Psychology
requirements.description: PSYC 1100. It may also be satisfied by a 5 on the Psychology AP test or a 7 on the IB Psychology exam.

requirements.name: Statistics
requirements.description: S&DS 1000 or S&DS 2300. A student with a 5 on the AP Statistics exam takes S&DS 2300 or S&DS 1230 instead. Preferably taken before senior year.

requirements.name: Social Science Courses
requirements.description: Two Psychology courses with the social science designation (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC Social Science). At least one must be a social science Core course: PSYC 1400, 1500 or 1700. Take the core course as early as possible in the major.

requirements.name: Natural Science Courses
requirements.description: Two Psychology courses with the natural science designation (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC Natural Science). At least one must be a natural science Core course: PSYC 1300 or 1600. Take the core course as early as possible in the major.

requirements.name: Research Methods
requirements.description: One Psychology course numbered 2000-2999, in which research is planned and carried out. Preferably taken before senior year. It cannot be taken Credit/D/Fail.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Four electives. With the permission of the DUS, up to three term courses in related departments may count toward the major, and they must have substantial empirical psychology content.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement: Seminar/Literature Review
requirements.description: Two course credits from PSYC 4000-4999. One of them must be from PSYC 4000-4899 or PSYC 4990, taken during the senior year for a letter grade, and carry a substantial final paper of at least 5,000 words. The B.A. is typically awarded for a nonempirical literature review; there is no restriction on the research format. No more than three credits from PSYC 4900-4999 may count toward the major.

PSYC_BS.name: Psychology, B.S.
PSYC_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Psychology. Emphasizes empirical research.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: Introduction to Psychology
requirements.description: PSYC 1100. It may also be satisfied by a 5 on the Psychology AP test or a 7 on the IB Psychology exam.

requirements.name: Statistics
requirements.description: S&DS 1000 or S&DS 2300. A student with a 5 on the AP Statistics exam takes S&DS 2300 or S&DS 1230 instead. Preferably taken before senior year.

requirements.name: Social Science Courses
requirements.description: Two Psychology courses with the social science designation (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC Social Science). At least one must be a social science Core course: PSYC 1400, 1500 or 1700. Take the core course as early as possible in the major.

requirements.name: Natural Science Courses
requirements.description: Two Psychology courses with the natural science designation (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC Natural Science). At least one must be a natural science Core course: PSYC 1300 or 1600. Take the core course as early as possible in the major.

requirements.name: Research Methods
requirements.description: One Psychology course numbered 2000-2999, in which research is planned and carried out. For the B.S. it must be taken before the senior year, and it cannot be taken Credit/D/Fail.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Four electives. With the permission of the DUS, up to three term courses in related departments may count toward the major, and they must have substantial empirical psychology content.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement: Empirical Research
requirements.description: PSYC 4990, taken during the senior year for a letter grade, in which the student designs an experiment and collects and analyses the data, plus one further course credit from PSYC 4000-4999. No more than three credits from PSYC 4900-4999 may count toward the major.

PSYC_BS_NEURO.name: Psychology, B.S. (Neuroscience Concentration)
PSYC_BS_NEURO.description: Bachelor of Science in Psychology with Neuroscience Concentration. Focus on behavioral, cellular, molecular, and cognitive neuroscience.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: Introduction to Psychology
requirements.description: PSYC 1100. It may also be satisfied by a 5 on the Psychology AP test or a 7 on the IB Psychology exam.

requirements.name: Biology Sequence
requirements.description: BIOL 1010, 1020, 1030 and 1040, half a credit each, unless excused by the Biology placement exam or a 5 on the Biology AP test or a 7 on the IB Biology exam.

requirements.name: Statistics
requirements.description: S&DS 1000 or S&DS 2300. A student with a 5 on the AP Statistics exam takes S&DS 2300 or S&DS 1230 instead. Preferably taken before senior year.

requirements.name: Social Science Courses
requirements.description: Two Psychology courses with the social science designation (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC Social Science). At least one must be a social science Core course: PSYC 1400, 1500 or 1700.

requirements.name: Neuroscience Core
requirements.description: PSYC 1600. MCDB 3200 or PSYC 2760 may substitute for it; if MCDB 3200 is substituted it cannot also count as one of the two advanced science courses.

requirements.name: Natural Science Course
requirements.description: One further Psychology course from the natural science list (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC Natural Science), beyond PSYC 1600 and the data-collection course.

requirements.name: Research Methods
requirements.description: One data-collection course (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC NSCI Track RsrchMthds). It cannot be taken Credit/D/Fail.

requirements.name: Advanced Science Courses
requirements.description: Two advanced science courses (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC NSCI Track Adv Scie) from MCDB and EEB courses numbered 2000 or above that deal with human or animal biology — recommended: MCDB 2000, 2020, 2050, 2100, 2500, 3000, 3150, 3200, EEB 2220, 2225. Some courses outside those departments also qualify, including BENG 3200, BENG 5440, CPSC 4750, MB&B 3000, 3010, 3520, 4200, 4350, 4430, MATH 2220, 2250 and 2410. Laboratory courses do not count.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement: Neuroscience Research
requirements.description: PSYC 4990, taken during the senior year as a neuroscientific empirical project supervised by a neuroscience faculty member in the department, plus one further course credit from PSYC 4000-4999. Both must have neuroscience content (Yale Course Search attribute YC PSYC NSCI Track Senior Sem).

requirements.name: Mathematics Requirement
requirements.description: One math course: MATH 1180 or 1200 preferred, or MATH 1120, 1150, 1160, ENAS 1510, or MATH 1100 and 1110 (which together count as one course). Any MATH course numbered 2000 or higher also satisfies the requirement.

requirements.name: Introductory Microeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 1108, 1110, or 1115. May be skipped or taken Credit/D/Fail on the basis of pre-college testing, in which case an extra elective is required.

requirements.name: Introductory Macroeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 1111 or 1116. May be skipped or taken Credit/D/Fail on the basis of pre-college testing, in which case an extra elective is required.

requirements.name: Intermediate Microeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 2121 or ECON 2125. May not be taken outside Yale.

requirements.name: Intermediate Macroeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 2122 or ECON 2126. May not be taken outside Yale.

requirements.name: Econometrics
requirements.description: ECON 1117, 2123, or 2136. ECON 2135 and the S&DS 2410/2420 pair are probability and statistics courses and do not satisfy this requirement on their own.

requirements.name: Economics Electives
requirements.description: Four electives: any ECON course numbered 2000 or above that is not already counted toward a core requirement. With DUS approval one non-Economics course related to economics may count. Take an additional elective for each introductory course you place out of or take Credit/D/Fail.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: Two ECON courses numbered 4400-4491 (advanced lectures 4440-4449 or senior seminars 4450-4490), at least one taken during the senior year. A senior essay is optional but required for Distinction in the Major.

MCDB_BA.name: Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology, B.A.
MCDB_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology. Broad training in biology spanning molecules to ecosystems. Prepares for biological, biomedical, health, and many professional careers.

requirements.name: Introductory Biology Sequence
requirements.description: BIOL 1010, 1020, 1030, and 1040 (half credit each, 2 credits in total). You may place out of modules by exam; with DUS permission, one MCDB core course substitutes for every two modules.

requirements.name: General Chemistry Sequence
requirements.description: A two-term chemistry lecture sequence, CHEM 1610 and CHEM 1650, or CHEM 1700 by placement. Acceleration credit in chemistry is accepted in place of it.

requirements.name: Mathematics or Statistics
requirements.description: MATH 1150 or higher, or S&DS 1000, 1080, 1090, or 2380. Other Yale statistics courses count with DUS approval, except S&DS 1600.

requirements.name: Physics
requirements.description: One term of physics, PHYS 1700 or above, usually in the junior year.

requirements.name: Core MCDB Courses
requirements.description: Two core courses from MCDB 2000, 2020, 2050, 2100, 2900, and 3000 (or MB&B 3000).

requirements.name: MCDB Electives (2000+)
requirements.description: Two MCDB courses numbered 2500 or above, or two more core courses from the list above. The paired laboratories MCDB 3420L and 3430L, or MCDB 3440L and 3450L, together count as one elective and then cannot also fill the laboratory requirement. A course used as a prerequisite cannot also count here.

requirements.name: Advanced MCDB Elective (3500+)
requirements.description: One MCDB course numbered 3500 or above. Independent research courses do not count. A course used elsewhere in the major cannot count here as well.

requirements.name: Biology Laboratory
requirements.description: One laboratory in the biological sciences from MCDB, MB&B, or Biomedical Engineering, or from Anthropology or Ecology and Evolutionary Biology with the DUS's permission. Independent research does not satisfy it.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement (no credit for essay option)
requirements.description: One term of individual research, MCDB 4750, in the senior year, or a 15-20 page senior essay evaluating current research in a field of biology. The essay carries no course credit.

MCDB_BS.name: Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology, B.S.
MCDB_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology. More intensive research and lab training. Prepares for advanced graduate or professional study.

requirements.name: Introductory Biology Sequence
requirements.description: BIOL 1010, 1020, 1030, and 1040 (half credit each, 2 credits in total). You may place out of modules by exam; with DUS permission, one MCDB core course substitutes for every two modules.

requirements.name: General Chemistry Sequence
requirements.description: A two-term chemistry lecture sequence, CHEM 1610 and CHEM 1650, or CHEM 1700 by placement. Acceleration credit in chemistry is accepted in place of it.

requirements.name: General Chemistry Laboratory
requirements.description: The laboratories that accompany the chemistry lecture sequence: CHEM 1340L and 1360L with CHEM 1610/1650, or CHEM 1710L with CHEM 1700 (half credit each).

requirements.name: Organic Chemistry
requirements.description: One term of organic chemistry: CHEM 1740, CHEM 1750, or CHEM 2200, usually in the sophomore year.

requirements.name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
requirements.description: The laboratory that accompanies organic chemistry: CHEM 2220L or CHEM 2230L (half credit).

requirements.name: Mathematics or Statistics
requirements.description: MATH 1150 or higher, or S&DS 1000, 1080, 1090, or 2380. Other Yale statistics courses count with DUS approval, except S&DS 1600.

requirements.name: Physics Sequence
requirements.description: A two-term physics lecture sequence numbered 1700 or above: PHYS 1700 and 1710, 1800 and 1810, 2000 and 2010, or 2600 and 2610. A physics laboratory is not required.

requirements.name: Core MCDB Courses
requirements.description: Three core courses from MCDB 2000, 2020, 2050, 2100, 2900, and 3000 (or MB&B 3000).

requirements.name: MCDB Electives (2000+)
requirements.description: Two MCDB courses numbered 2500 or above. Additional core courses, a second term of organic chemistry, or a statistics course may substitute, as may the paired laboratories MCDB 3420L and 3430L or MCDB 3440L and 3450L, which together count as one elective and then cannot also fill the laboratory requirement. A course used as a prerequisite cannot also count here.

requirements.name: Advanced MCDB Elective (3500+)
requirements.description: One MCDB course numbered 3500 or above. Independent research courses do not count. A course used elsewhere in the major cannot count here as well.

requirements.name: MCDB Laboratory
requirements.description: Two half-credit MCDB laboratories from MCDB 2010L, 2030L, 2210L, 2310L, 2510L, 2910L, 3030L, 3210L, 3410L, 3420L, 3430L, 3440L, and 3450L. Independent research does not satisfy a laboratory requirement.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: Two consecutive terms of independent research in the senior year, MCDB 4850 and MCDB 4860, with at least ten hours a week in the lab.

MCDB_BS_INTENSIVE.name: Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology, B.S. Intensive
MCDB_BS_INTENSIVE.description: B.S. Intensive: For highly motivated students with advanced research focus, including extended senior research experience.

requirements.name: General Chemistry Sequence

requirements.name: General Chemistry Laboratory

requirements.name: Organic Chemistry

requirements.name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
requirements.description: The laboratory that accompanies organic chemistry: CHEM 2220L or CHEM 2230L (half credit).

requirements.name: Mathematics or Statistics
requirements.description: MATH 1150 or higher, or S&DS 1000, 1080, 1090, or 2380. Other Yale statistics courses count with DUS approval, except S&DS 1600.

requirements.name: Physics Sequence
requirements.description: A two-term physics lecture sequence numbered 1700 or above: PHYS 1700 and 1710, 1800 and 1810, 2000 and 2010, or 2600 and 2610. A physics laboratory is not required.

requirements.name: Core MCDB Courses
requirements.description: Three core courses from MCDB 2000, 2020, 2050, 2100, 2900, and 3000 (or MB&B 3000).

requirements.name: MCDB Electives (2000+)
requirements.description: Two MCDB courses numbered 2500 or above. Additional core courses, a second term of organic chemistry, or a statistics course may substitute, as may the paired laboratories MCDB 3420L and 3430L or MCDB 3440L and 3450L, which together count as one elective and then cannot also fill the laboratory requirement. A course used as a prerequisite cannot also count here.

requirements.name: Advanced MCDB Elective (3500+)
requirements.description: One MCDB course numbered 3500 or above. Independent research courses do not count. A course used elsewhere in the major cannot count here as well.

requirements.name: MCDB Laboratory
requirements.description: Two half-credit MCDB laboratories from MCDB 2010L, 2030L, 2210L, 2310L, 2510L, 2910L, 3030L, 3210L, 3410L, 3420L, 3430L, 3440L, and 3450L. Independent research does not satisfy a laboratory requirement.

requirements.name: Senior Research Intensive
requirements.description: Two terms of senior research, MCDB 4950 and MCDB 4960, worth two credits each, with at least twenty hours a week in the lab.

TDPS_BA.name: Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies, B.A.
TDPS_BA.description: B.A. in Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies: a flexible, interdisciplinary program in theater, dance, and performance, including history, theory, and creative practice.

requirements.name: Collaboration (Prerequisite)
requirements.description: TDPS 1000, Collaboration. Prerequisite for the major; it may be taken concurrently with term courses. Counts toward the total.

requirements.name: Introduction to Theater, Dance, and Performance (Prerequisite)
requirements.description: TDPS 1001, Modes of Performance. Prerequisite for the major; it may be taken concurrently with term courses. Counts toward the total.

requirements.name: Artistic Practice Domain
requirements.description: Two courses in Artistic Practice (YC TDPS Artistic Practice attribute): techniques and compositional strategies in theater, dance, musical theater, design, and intermedia performance. Most courses are listed in more than one domain but may count for only one domain requirement.

requirements.name: Interarts Domain
requirements.description: Two courses in Interarts (YC TDPS Interarts attribute): art-making between disciplines, including work that puts the performing arts in conversation with film, visual art, new media, psychology, or science. Most courses are listed in more than one domain but may count for only one domain requirement.

requirements.name: Histories Domain
requirements.description: Two courses in Histories (YC TDPS Histories attribute): study defined by period, genre, or geographic region, including performance-based historical research. Most courses are listed in more than one domain but may count for only one domain requirement.

requirements.name: Performance Theory Domain
requirements.description: Two courses in Performance Theory (YC TDPS Performance Theory attribute): foundational theories of performativity and theatricality. Most courses are listed in more than one domain but may count for only one domain requirement.

requirements.name: Related Elective
requirements.description: One related elective (YC TDPS Elective). Any TDPS course counts except the prerequisites (TDPS 1000 and 1001), the independent study TDPS 4701, and the senior requirement courses (TDPS 4900, 4901, 4902). Courses from other departments carrying a TDPS domain attribute also count.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: One of five routes, with the approval of the DUS: a substantial senior essay written in an upper-level seminar, a production seminar, TDPS 4900 (Senior Independent Study), TDPS 4901 (Senior Project, which also requires a 15-25 page essay), or TDPS 4902 (Senior Seminar, a 35-50 page essay or writing portfolio). The seminar and production-seminar routes are ordinary courses taken with higher expectations, so they cannot be recognised from a course code.

EECS.name: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, B.S.
EECS.description: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS). A comprehensive program covering both electrical engineering and computer science fundamentals, preparing students for careers in technology and engineering.

requirements.name: Calculus I
requirements.description: MATH 1120. This prerequisite may be waived for students who have taken the equivalent of one year of calculus in high school. Acceleration credits may not be used to satisfy prerequisites.

requirements.name: Calculus II
requirements.description: MATH 1150, which may be waived for a year of high-school calculus. MATH 1160 may not be substituted.

requirements.name: Multivariable Calculus (Calc III)
requirements.description: ENAS 1510 or MATH 1200, or a higher-level course. MATH 1210 may not be substituted for MATH 1200.

requirements.name: Intro Programming (if needed)
requirements.description: CPSC 1001, required only for students without previous programming experience.

requirements.name: Physics I
requirements.description: First term of the physics prerequisite: PHYS 1800 or PHYS 2000, taken as a sequence with the second term. PHYS 1700 is acceptable for students taking MATH 1120, but the Electrical Engineering and Engineering Sciences (Electrical) B.S. programs do not allow that substitution.

requirements.name: Physics II
requirements.description: Second term of the physics prerequisite, from the same sequence as the first: PHYS 1810 with PHYS 1800, PHYS 2010 with PHYS 2000, or PHYS 1710 with PHYS 1700.

requirements.name: Mathematical Tools for CS
requirements.description: CPSC 2020, or MATH 2440 as a substitute.

requirements.name: Algorithms
requirements.description: CPSC 3650 or CPSC 3660. Only one of the two may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Advanced Math/Stats Requirement
requirements.description: One of MATH 2220, MATH 2250, MATH 2260, S&DS 2380 or S&DS 2410.

requirements.name: Advanced ECE Elective 1
requirements.description: A 3000- or 4000-level Electrical Engineering course. Cross-titled courses may be counted either way. With permission of both DUSs, one of ECE 4680 or ECE 4691 may be used as an electrical engineering elective.

requirements.name: Advanced ECE Elective 2
requirements.description: A second 3000- or 4000-level Electrical Engineering course, or another advanced course approved by the DUS of each department.

requirements.name: Advanced CPSC Elective 1
requirements.description: A 3000- or 4000-level Computer Science course. CPSC 2900 and CPSC 4900 may not be used as electives.

requirements.name: Advanced CPSC Elective 2
requirements.description: A second 3000- or 4000-level Computer Science course, or another advanced course approved by the DUS of each department.

requirements.name: Senior Project
requirements.description: Independent senior project in CPSC 4900, or in ECE 4710 and/or ECE 4721, depending on your adviser's department. It must be approved by the DUS in each department.

RLST_BA.name: Religious Studies, B.A.
RLST_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies. Interdisciplinary exploration of religious traditions, systems, texts, practices, and critical methodologies.

requirements.name: Core RLST Courses
requirements.description: Five courses that carry the RLST subject code, chosen with the DUS: one introductory course numbered 0001-1999, one that brings breadth to your core area, and three that form a cohesive group leading to your senior essay topic. The engine cannot check that structure, only that five RLST courses are done.

requirements.name: Junior Seminar
requirements.description: RLST 4900, Religion and Society, normally taken in the junior year. It may not be taken Credit/D/Fail.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Four electives that complement your area of expertise, chosen with DUS approval, inside or outside the department: language study, methods from other disciplines, further advanced RLST coursework, or Divinity School courses. Up to two courses counted toward another major or certificate may also count here.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: The two-term senior essay, RLST 4910 and RLST 4920, written across both terms of senior year under a faculty adviser in your core area. It counts as two courses toward the major.

requirements.name: Introductory Physics Sequence
requirements.description: Two courses: one complete lecture sequence, either PHYS 1700 and 1710, or PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010. Both halves must come from the same sequence, and each sequence has its own math corequisites.

requirements.name: Calculus I
requirements.description: MATH 1120.

requirements.name: Calculus II
requirements.description: MATH 1150.

requirements.name: Calculus III
requirements.description: Either MATH 1200 or ENAS 1510. All prerequisites should be finished by the end of sophomore year.

requirements.name: Fundamentals of Astronomy
requirements.description: Either ASTR 2100 or ASTR 2200. The two overlap in content, so take one of them, not both.

requirements.name: Research Methods in Astrophysics
requirements.description: ASTR 2550, which covers data analysis, computer programming and statistical methods.

requirements.name: Galactic and Extragalactic Astronomy
requirements.description: ASTR 3100.

requirements.name: Astronomy Elective (2000+)
requirements.description: One further Astronomy course numbered 2000 or above, beyond ASTR 2100/2200, ASTR 2550, ASTR 3100 and the senior project. Courses numbered 3000 or above assume ASTR 2100 or 2200, multivariable calculus and two terms of college physics. ASTR 3560 may be used here or as one of the two advanced mathematics courses, but not for both.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement (Essay/Project)
requirements.description: One term of ASTR 4920: a senior essay or independent research project supervised by a faculty member.

requirements.name: Advanced Mathematics or Mathematical Methods
requirements.description: Two advanced courses in mathematics or mathematical methods, including statistics or computer science: a MATH course numbered 2000 or above, or ASTR 3560. Approved by the director of undergraduate studies.

requirements.name: Science Electives
requirements.description: Three electives from the natural, applied or mathematical sciences, which may include further astronomy courses. At least two of the three must be numbered 3000 or above.

requirements.name: Introductory Physics Sequence
requirements.description: Two courses: one complete lecture sequence, either PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010, or PHYS 2600 and 2610. Both halves must come from the same sequence, and each sequence has its own math corequisites.

requirements.name: Physics Laboratory Sequence
requirements.description: Two terms of laboratory: PHYS 1650L and 1660L, or PHYS 2050L and 2060L. ASTR 1550 may be substituted for one of the two terms. Both halves should come from the same sequence, and each course is worth half a credit.

requirements.name: Calculus I
requirements.description: MATH 1120.

requirements.name: Calculus II
requirements.description: MATH 1150.

requirements.name: Calculus III

requirements.description: Either ASTR 2100 or ASTR 2200. The two overlap in content, so take one of them, not both.

requirements.name: Research Methods in Astrophysics
requirements.description: ASTR 2550, which covers data analysis, computer programming and statistical methods.

requirements.name: Galactic and Extragalactic Astronomy
requirements.description: ASTR 3100.

requirements.name: Physical Processes in Astronomy
requirements.description: ASTR 3200.

requirements.name: Physics Courses (4000+)
requirements.description: Three Physics courses numbered 4000 or above, normally PHYS 4010, PHYS 4020 and PHYS 4390. PHYS 4000 is not counted here because it is one of the differential equations options.

requirements.name: Physics/Astronomy Advanced Elective
requirements.description: One additional course in Physics numbered 4000 or above, or in Astronomy numbered 3000 or above. It must be a fourth course beyond the three Physics courses above; no course may be counted for two requirements.

requirements.name: Differential Equations
requirements.description: One course in differential equations: MATH 2460, PHYS 4000 or ENAS 1940.

requirements.name: Math/Statistics/Computing
requirements.description: One further mathematics course numbered 2000 or above, or a course in statistics or computing such as CPSC 2010 or ASTR 3560.

requirements.name: Senior Project I
requirements.description: First term of the two-term senior research project in astronomy, supervised by a faculty member.

requirements.name: Senior Project II
requirements.description: Second term of the two-term senior research project in astronomy.

APHY_BS.name: Applied Physics, B.S.
APHY_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Applied Physics

requirements.name: Physics Courses
requirements.description: Two courses: one complete introductory lecture sequence, either PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010, or PHYS 2600 and 2610. Both halves must come from the same sequence, and each sequence has its own math corequisites. PHYS 2000 and 2010 are the recommended starting point.

requirements.name: Physics Lab
requirements.description: One physics laboratory course, PHYS 1660L or PHYS 2060L, normally taken in the first or second year. Each is worth half a credit, and each is the second term of a lab sequence (PHYS 1650L precedes 1660L, PHYS 2050L precedes 2060L).

requirements.name: Multivariable Calculus
requirements.description: APHY 1510 or MATH 1200.

requirements.name: Advanced Math & Physics
requirements.description: PHYS 4000, or APHY 1940 taken together with a linear algebra course (MATH 2220, MATH 2250 or MATH 2260).

requirements.name: Core Applied Physics
requirements.description: APHY 3220, Electromagnetic Waves and Devices, or an equivalent approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Quantum Mechanics
requirements.description: APHY 4390 (cross-listed as PHYS 4390) or PHYS 4400, or an equivalent approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Applied Physics Topics
requirements.description: APHY 4200, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, or an equivalent approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Area of Focus Courses
requirements.description: Three advanced courses in the physical or mathematical sciences or engineering that together form an area of focus, approved by the DUS. For example APHY 4480, APHY 4490, ECE 3200 and ECE 3250 for quantum electronics, or APHY 4480, APHY 4490, CHEM 2200 and MENG 2615 for materials and nanoscience. The electives should relate to the senior research topic.

requirements.name: Senior Research Project I
requirements.description: First term of the independent research project, supervised by a faculty member in Applied Physics, Physics, Engineering or a related department. Must be taken for a letter grade; may be started in the junior year.

requirements.name: Senior Research Project II
requirements.description: Second term of the independent research project. Must be taken for a letter grade.

EVST_BA.name: Environmental Studies, B.A.
EVST_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies

requirements.name: Prereq: Statistics
requirements.description: One course in statistics or data science, S&DS 1000 or higher. Completing the Certificate in Data Science also satisfies this prerequisite, which no single course code can represent.

requirements.name: Core: Humanities or Social Sciences
requirements.description: Two core courses: one in the humanities and one in the social sciences, from the approved lists on the Environmental Studies website (Yale Course Search attributes YC EVST Core Humanities and YC EVST Core Social Sci).

requirements.name: Core: Natural Sciences
requirements.description: Three core courses, one in each natural science category: life science and ecology; earth and climate science; and physical science, technology and environment (Yale Course Search attributes YC EVST Core BA Life Sci, YC EVST Core BA Climate Sci, YC EVST Core BA Physical Sci).

requirements.name: Concentration Courses
requirements.description: Six courses giving analytical depth in one environmental problem, planned with the DUS. One must be an advanced seminar (YC EVST Advanced Seminar); a second must be either another advanced seminar or an intermediate or higher-level course in quantitative research methods (YC EVST BA QR Methods).

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: One term of EVST 4960, the colloquium in which the senior essay is written. A two-term senior research project is possible instead, with the permission of the DUS obtained before the end of junior year.

requirements.name: Senior Advanced Seminar
requirements.description: Students writing the one-term senior essay must also take an additional advanced seminar with an environmental focus. It is beyond the six concentration courses. Students approved for a two-term research project take the second term of EVST 4960 in its place.

EVST_BS.name: Environmental Studies, B.S.
EVST_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Studies

requirements.name: Prereq: Statistics, Math, or Physics
requirements.description: One term course in mathematics, physics or statistics: MATH 1120 or higher, PHYS 1700 or higher, or S&DS 1000 or higher. Completing the Certificate in Data Science also satisfies this prerequisite, which no single course code can represent.

requirements.name: Prereq: Chemistry Sequence
requirements.description: The two-term chemistry lecture sequence. Students who qualify for advanced placement in chemistry may instead take one term of CHEM 1670 or higher.

requirements.name: Prereq: Biology Sequence
requirements.description: The two-credit biology sequence BIOL 1010, 1020, 1030 and 1040, each worth half a credit.

requirements.name: Prereq: Natural Science Lab
requirements.description: One natural science laboratory from the list on the Environmental Studies website (Yale Course Search attribute YC EVST BS Natural Sci Lab).

requirements.name: Core: Humanities or Social Sciences
requirements.description: Two core courses: one in the humanities and one in the social sciences, from the approved lists on the Environmental Studies website (Yale Course Search attributes YC EVST Core Humanities and YC EVST Core Social Sci).

requirements.name: Core: Natural Sciences
requirements.description: Two natural science core courses from the approved list (Yale Course Search attribute YC EVST Core BS Natural Sci).

requirements.name: Concentration Courses
requirements.description: Six courses giving analytical depth in one environmental problem, planned with the DUS. Three must carry the science (SC) distributional designation and be numbered 2000 or higher, and two must provide interdisciplinary context.

requirements.name: Elective
requirements.description: One elective course relevant to the major.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: EVST 4960, the senior research project and colloquium. The B.S. senior requirement is two terms of EVST 4960; the first term is counted here.

requirements.name: Senior Research Project, Second Term
requirements.description: The second term of EVST 4960. It is the same course code as the first term, so it has to be marked as fulfilled by hand.

RUSS_BA.name: Russian, B.A.
RUSS_BA.description: B.A. in Russian language, literature, and culture, with advanced coursework in Russian and Russian literature, including literary analysis, history, and cultural context.

requirements.name: Language prereq
requirements.description: Prerequisite to the major is second-year Russian: RUSS 1400, RUSS 1420, or RUSS 1450. The placement exam, an approved summer intensive, or study abroad may satisfy it instead. The prerequisite is not one of the 11 courses of the major.

requirements.name: Third-Year Russian
requirements.description: RUSS 1500 and RUSS 1510 (1.5 credits each).

requirements.name: Fourth-Year Russian
requirements.description: RUSS 1600 and RUSS 1610.

requirements.name: 19th-century or earlier Russian Literature in Translation
requirements.description: One course in 19th-century or earlier Russian literature in translation. Russian First-Year Seminars and Russian courses numbered 2000 or higher may fulfill this requirement; which term counts depends on the period covered, so add the course by hand.

requirements.name: 20th-century or later Russian Literature in Translation
requirements.description: One course in 20th-century or later Russian literature in translation. Russian First-Year Seminars and Russian courses numbered 2000 or higher may fulfill this requirement; which term counts depends on the period covered, so add the course by hand.

requirements.name: Content Course Taught in Russian
requirements.description: One content course in which Russian is the language of instruction (RUSS 1700-1900). Offerings vary by year; any course in that range counts.

requirements.name: Russian, East European, or Eurasian History or Social Sciences
requirements.description: One course in Russian, East European, or Eurasian history or social sciences, drawn from any department.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Electives as needed to bring the major to 11 term courses. Yale summer program courses in Russian culture (RUSS S241, S242, S243) may substitute with DUS approval.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: RUSS 4900 or RUSS 4910. All primary sources used in the essay must be read in Russian. Students may enrol in both, but only one counts toward the major.

AFST.name: African Studies, B.A.
AFST.description: Bachelor of Arts in African Studies: twelve term courses covering humanities and social science work on Africa, two years of an African language, a research methods course, an area of focus, and the senior essay.

requirements.name: AFST Humanities Course
requirements.description: One African Studies course in the humanities. The catalog names no specific course, so choose one with the DUS and record it here.

requirements.name: AFST Social Science Course
requirements.description: One African Studies course in the social sciences. The catalog names no specific course, so choose one with the DUS and record it here.

requirements.name: African Language Study
requirements.description: Two years (four terms) of an African language — Kiswahili, Twi, Wolof, Yorùbá, isiZulu, Arabic, or another with DUS permission. The requirement can be waived by placement into an advanced course or an equivalent test through the Center for Language Study; if waived, substitute four additional African Studies courses.

requirements.name: Research Methods
requirements.description: One research methods course: the graduate course AFST 5505, or an alternative that deepens the area of focus or supplies methodological tools for the senior essay, selected with the DUS. AFST 5505 is a graduate course and is not in DI's undergraduate course catalog, so record whichever course you take here.

requirements.name: Focus Area Courses
requirements.description: Four courses in a chosen area of focus — a discipline such as anthropology, art history, history, languages and literature, political science, or sociology; an interdisciplinary program such as Black Studies, Ethnicity, Race, and Migration, or Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies; or a cross-disciplinary area such as diaspora or development studies. Other areas need DUS approval first.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: AFST 4491, the senior essay, written with a faculty adviser. A preliminary statement of topic and adviser is due to the DUS by the end of the second week of the fall term senior year.

EPS_BA.name: Earth and Planetary Sciences, B.A.
EPS_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Earth and Planetary Sciences

requirements.name: Math Prereq
requirements.description: MATH 1150 (calculus through Calculus II). MATH 1120 is a prerequisite for MATH 1150.

requirements.name: Bio or Physics Prereq
requirements.description: Either biology (BIOL 1010 and 1020) or physics (PHYS 1700 and 1710, or PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010). Both halves must come from the same sequence; the biology courses are half a credit each.

requirements.name: Chemistry Prereq
requirements.description: Any chemistry lecture course.

requirements.name: Introductory EPS Courses (with labs)
requirements.description: Two introductory courses in Earth and Planetary Sciences numbered EPS 1000-1400, together with any accompanying laboratory. EPS 1100 carries the lab EPS 1110L and EPS 1250 carries the lab EPS 1260L; the labs are extra half-credit courses and are not counted here.

requirements.name: EPS Core: Natural Resources
requirements.description: Either EPS 2740 or EPS 2750.

requirements.name: EPS Core: Geochemical Processes
requirements.description: One of EPS 2200, EPS 2320, EPS 2610 or EPS 3100.

requirements.name: Upper-level EPS Courses
requirements.description: Four additional courses at the 2000 level or higher in Earth and Planetary Sciences; courses in related fields count with DUS approval. These four plus the senior requirement are the five additional upper-level courses the catalog asks for.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: The senior essay EPS 4920, or, with the consent of the faculty, a two-term senior thesis (EPS 4900 and EPS 4910). The thesis takes two terms; only one course is counted here.

EPS_BS_ATMOCEANCLIM.name: Earth and Planetary Sciences, B.S. – Atmosphere, Ocean, and Climate Concentration
EPS_BS_ATMOCEANCLIM.description: Comprehensive study of the atmosphere-ocean-climate system: climate change, meteorology, oceanography, fluid mechanics, and statistics.

requirements.name: Math Prereq
requirements.description: MATH 1200 or ENAS 1510 (mathematics through multivariable calculus).

requirements.name: Applied Math/Engineering Prereqs
requirements.description: ENAS 1300 (or equivalent computing course) and ENAS 1940 (differential equations).

requirements.name: Physics Prereq
requirements.description: PHYS 1800 and 1810, plus the laboratories PHYS 2050L and 2060L. The two laboratories are half a credit each.

requirements.name: Introductory EPS Course
requirements.description: One introductory course: EPS 1000, EPS 1010, EPS 1100 with its lab EPS 1110L, or EPS 1250 with its lab EPS 1260L. EPS 1000 and EPS 1010 need no lab; the labs are extra half-credit courses and are not counted here.

requirements.name: EPS Core Courses
requirements.description: Five core courses: EPS 1400, EPS 3350, MENG 3422, one of EPS 3220 or EPS 3230, and one of S&DS 2300, S&DS 2380 or MATH 2220. Other higher-level EPS courses may be substituted with the permission of the DUS.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Four electives chosen from topics in the environment, processes of the atmosphere, ocean, land surface, physics, and statistics. At least one must be from EPS. A list of suggested electives is available from the DUS.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: The senior essay EPS 4920, or, with the consent of the faculty, a two-term senior thesis (EPS 4900 and EPS 4910). The thesis takes two terms; only one course is counted here.

EPS_BS_ENV_ENERGY.name: Earth and Planetary Sciences, B.S. – Environmental and Energy Geoscience Concentration
EPS_BS_ENV_ENERGY.description: Focuses on natural and anthropogenic processes that shape the Earth-atmosphere-biosphere system and energy/material flows.

requirements.name: Chemistry Prereq
requirements.description: CHEM 1650 or CHEM 1670 (Advanced General Chemistry II).

requirements.name: Math Prereq
requirements.description: MATH 1200 or ENAS 1510 (mathematics through multivariable calculus).

requirements.name: Biology or Physics Prereq
requirements.description: Either physics (PHYS 1700 and 1710, or PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010) or biology: cellular biology (BIOL 1010 and 1020) together with evolutionary biology (BIOL 1030 and 1040, or EPS 1250 and EPS 1260L). The biology route is four half-credit courses, so finishing it means more than the two courses shown here.

requirements.name: Introductory EPS Courses
requirements.description: Two introductory courses: EPS 1000, EPS 1010, EPS 1100 with its lab EPS 1110L, EPS 1250 with its lab EPS 1260L, or EPS 1400. The labs are extra half-credit courses and are not counted here.

requirements.name: EPS Core Courses
requirements.description: Four core courses, each from a different area: geology (EPS 2100, EPS 2200 or EPS 3120), Earth surface processes (EPS 2320), geomicrobiology (EPS 2550), fossil fuels (EPS 2740), renewable energy (EPS 2750), geochemical principles (EPS 3100), climate (EPS 3220 or EPS 3230), and satellite image analysis (EPS 3620). Other higher-level EPS courses may be substituted with the permission of the DUS.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Four electives from Earth and Planetary Sciences, Environmental Studies, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Engineering or related fields; at least two must be from EPS. Electives may be chosen from the core course list.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: The senior essay EPS 4920, or, with the consent of the faculty, a two-term senior thesis (EPS 4900 and EPS 4910). The thesis takes two terms; only one course is counted here.

EPS_BS_PALEOGEO.name: Earth and Planetary Sciences, B.S. – Paleontology and Geobiology Concentration
EPS_BS_PALEOGEO.description: Focuses on the fossil record of life, geochemical imprints, and interactions between life and Earth. Integrates paleontology, geochemistry, and evolutionary biology.

requirements.name: Biology/Chemistry/Math Prereqs
requirements.description: College-level biology BIOL 1010, 1020, 1030 and 1040 (half a credit each); CHEM 1650 or CHEM 1670 (Advanced General Chemistry II); and mathematics through multivariable calculus, MATH 1200 or ENAS 1510.

requirements.name: Introductory EPS Course
requirements.description: One of EPS 1000, EPS 1010, or EPS 1100 with its lab EPS 1110L. The lab is an extra half-credit course and is not counted here.

requirements.name: Introduction to the Fossil Record
requirements.description: Both EPS 1250 and its laboratory EPS 1260L, worth 1.5 credits together.

requirements.name: Core Courses
requirements.description: Four core courses, each from a different area: sedimentary processes (EPS 2320 or EPS 3550), evolution (EEB 2225), vertebrate paleontology (EPS 3250), paleoecology (EPS 3450), geomicrobiology (EPS 2550), geochemical processes (EPS 3100), or a statistical data analysis course approved by the DUS. Other higher-level EPS courses may be substituted with the permission of the DUS.

requirements.name: Upper-level Paleontology Electives
requirements.description: Four electives from Earth and Planetary Sciences, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Molecular, Cellular and Developmental Biology or related fields. They should be upper-level (2000 or above) paleontology courses, and at least one must be from EPS.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: The senior essay EPS 4920, or, with the consent of the faculty, a two-term senior thesis (EPS 4900 and EPS 4910). The thesis takes two terms; only one course is counted here.

EPS_BS_SOLIDEARTH.name: Earth and Planetary Sciences, B.S. – Solid Earth Science Concentration
EPS_BS_SOLIDEARTH.description: Integrates geological, geochemical, and geophysical approaches to study Earth's interior, tectonics, and surface processes.

requirements.name: Chemistry Prereq
requirements.description: CHEM 1650 or CHEM 1670 (Advanced General Chemistry II).

requirements.name: Math Prereq
requirements.description: MATH 1200 or ENAS 1510 (mathematics through multivariable calculus).

requirements.name: Physics Prereq
requirements.description: One complete physics sequence: PHYS 1700 and 1710, or PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010. Both halves must come from the same sequence.

requirements.name: Introductory EPS Courses
requirements.description: Two introductory courses: EPS 1000, EPS 1010, EPS 1100 with its lab EPS 1110L, EPS 1250 with its lab EPS 1260L, or EPS 1400. The labs are extra half-credit courses and are not counted here.

requirements.name: Core Courses
requirements.description: Four core courses, each from a different area: mountain building and global tectonics (EPS 2100, EPS 2120 or EPS 3500), rocks and minerals (EPS 2200), sedimentary rocks and processes (EPS 2320), isotope geochemistry (EPS 3100), and structural geology (EPS 3120). Other higher-level EPS courses may be substituted with the permission of the DUS.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Four electives in geology, geochemistry, geophysics or related topics. At least two must be from EPS. Electives may be chosen from the core course list.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: The senior essay EPS 4920, or, with the consent of the faculty, a two-term senior thesis (EPS 4900 and EPS 4910). The thesis takes two terms; only one course is counted here.

CPSC_PSYCH_BS.name: Computer Science and Psychology, B.A.
CPSC_PSYCH_BS.description: The Computer Science and Psychology interdepartmental major at Yale integrates foundational knowledge and approaches from both disciplines. The major requires 14 term courses (beyond the prerequisite) plus a senior project, distributed across Computer Science (including advanced AI) and Psychology (including research methods and statistics).

requirements.name: Introduction to Psychology
requirements.description: Prerequisite for the major. Waived for a score of 5 on the AP Psychology exam.

requirements.name: Mathematical Tools for Computer Science
requirements.description: CPSC 2020, or MATH 2440 as a substitute.

requirements.name: Systems Programming and Computer Organization
requirements.description: CPSC 3230, one of the five required core Computer Science courses.

requirements.name: Algorithms
requirements.description: CPSC 3650 or CPSC 3660. Only one of the two may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Advanced CS Artificial Intelligence
requirements.description: Three advanced Computer Science courses in artificial intelligence, for example those in the range CPSC 4700-4770, CPSC 4520, CPSC 4530, or CPSC 4810-4890. CPSC 2800 and CPSC 4900 may not be counted. With permission of both DUSs, one highly relevant course in cognitive psychology or cognitive science may substitute for one of the three.

requirements.name: Statistics
requirements.description: One statistics course: S&DS 1000 or S&DS 2300. This is one of the six Psychology-side courses.

requirements.name: Psychology Research Methods
requirements.description: At least one research methods course from PSYC 2100-2990. No 2000-level Psychology course taken Credit/D/Fail may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Psychology Social Science Courses
requirements.description: Two Psychology courses from the social science point of view; at least one must be designated a Core course in the course listings.

requirements.name: Psychology Natural Science Courses
requirements.description: Two Psychology courses from the natural science point of view; at least one must be designated a Core course in the course listings.

requirements.name: Senior Project
requirements.description: Senior requirement: CPSC 4900 or PSYC 4990. The project must be approved by the DUS in each department.

GLBL_BA.name: Global Affairs, B.A.
GLBL_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Global Affairs. Fourteen courses including the eight introductory courses required to declare the major and the senior requirement, plus an L4 course in a modern language other than English, which the catalog does not count among the fourteen.

requirements.name: Introductory Microeconomics
requirements.description: One of ECON 1108, ECON 1110, or ECON 1115. Part of the eight introductory courses needed to declare the major.

requirements.name: Introductory Macroeconomics
requirements.description: One of ECON 1111 or ECON 1116. Part of the eight introductory courses needed to declare the major.

requirements.name: Introductory Political Science (International Relations, Comparative Politics, or Political Theory)
requirements.description: Two introductory Political Science courses from different subdisciplines: PLSC 1113 (international relations), PLSC 1413 (comparative politics), or a political theory course — PLSC 1327, PLSC 1335, PLSC 1352, DRST 0005, DRST 0006, or PHIL 1178. The two must come from different subdisciplines, which this list cannot enforce.

requirements.name: History Courses
requirements.description: Two History courses — any course with a HIST number, enrolling under the HIST number if the course is cross-listed.

requirements.name: Applied Quantitative Analysis I
requirements.description: GLBL 2121, ideally taken in the fall of sophomore year. It may not also count as an elective.

requirements.name: Advanced Course (Game Theory, Intermediate Economics, or Qualitative Methods)
requirements.description: One advanced course: game theory (GLBL 2159 / ECON 2259), intermediate microeconomics (ECON 2121), intermediate macroeconomics (ECON 2122), or an approved qualitative methods course carrying the YC GLBL Qualitative Methods attribute. Part of the eight introductory courses; a qualitative methods course has no fixed number, so record it manually.

requirements.name: Applied Quantitative Analysis II
requirements.description: GLBL 2122, required beyond the introductory courses. It may not also count as an elective.

requirements.name: Challenges in Global Affairs
requirements.description: GLBL 3101.

requirements.name: Global Affairs Electives
requirements.description: Three electives carrying the YC GLBL Elective attribute, from Global Affairs, History, Political Science, Economics, or other approved departments. At most two of the three may be taught by Senior Fellows (the YC GLBL Senior Fellow Elective attribute).

requirements.name: Language Requirement (L4)
requirements.description: One course designated L4 in a modern language other than English. It is required of every major but is not one of the fourteen courses the catalog counts; a Cr grade in an L4 course may be used to demonstrate proficiency. L4 courses exist in many languages and have no shared code, so record the one you take here.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: One of: the Capstone policy task force GLBL 4499 (offered only in the fall of senior year); a senior essay in a substantive seminar of the student's choosing; or a senior essay in GLBL 4500. On the seminar route the student secures their own adviser and second reader, and records the seminar here manually.

ARCG_BA.name: Archaeological Studies, B.A.
ARCG_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Archaeological Studies

requirements.name: Introductory Survey
requirements.description: One introductory survey course approved for the major; the approved list is published on Yale Course Search under the attribute YC ARCG Intro Survey.

requirements.name: Introductory Laboratory
requirements.description: ARCG 3116L, Introduction to Archaeological Laboratory Sciences.

requirements.name: Advanced Laboratory
requirements.description: One advanced laboratory course, separate from ARCG 3116L; the approved list is published on Yale Course Search under the attribute YC ARCG Advanced Lab.

requirements.name: Theory Course
requirements.description: One archaeological theory course; the approved list is published on Yale Course Search under the attribute YC ARCG Theory.

requirements.name: Electives (as approved by DUS)
requirements.description: Seven electives distributed among the subject areas of the departments that cross-list with Archaeological Studies (Anthropology, Classics, Earth and Planetary Sciences, Environmental Studies, History, History of Art, Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations, Religious Studies), with three of the seven in three different departments. With DUS permission, three of them may be courses from other departments related to your research.

requirements.name: Summer Fieldwork or Research
requirements.description: Participation in at least one intensive summer field school: a Yale-affiliated archaeological research project, or another field school approved in advance by the DUS. This is not a course credit and does not count toward the twelve courses.

requirements.name: Senior Research Project
requirements.description: ARCG 4491, a senior research project in some field of archaeology, preferably one involving more than one area or discipline.

PORT_BA.name: Portuguese, B.A.
PORT_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Portuguese. Prepares students for advanced proficiency in Portuguese language, literatures, and cultures.

requirements.name: Language Prerequisite
requirements.description: PORT 1300, Intermediate Portuguese I, or the equivalent by placement. The prerequisite is not one of the ten courses for the major.

requirements.name: Courses in Portuguese World Literatures or Cultures
requirements.description: At least 5 term courses in the literatures or cultures of the Portuguese world.

requirements.name: Related Courses (Outside PORT)
requirements.description: Four more term courses to reach ten beyond the prerequisite. With DUS approval up to 4 of them may be taken outside the department — in other languages and literatures, anthropology, history, or history of art — or on study abroad.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: Senior essay, written in PORT 4910 and/or PORT 4920. A maximum of two credits of senior essay counts toward the major.

AMTH_BA.name: Applied Mathematics, B.A.
AMTH_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Applied Mathematics

requirements.name: Computer Programming
requirements.description: Programming is a prerequisite for the major and can be met with either ENAS 1300 or CPSC 1001. It does not count toward the courses required beyond the prerequisites.

requirements.name: Multivariable Calculus
requirements.description: Prerequisite, to be taken before or during sophomore year: MATH 1200 or ENAS 1510, or the equivalent.

requirements.name: Linear Algebra
requirements.description: Prerequisite, to be taken before or during sophomore year: MATH 2220 (cross-listed as AMTH 2220), MATH 2250 or MATH 2260.

requirements.name: Differential Equations
requirements.description: One differential equations course: ENAS 1940 or MATH 2460.

requirements.name: Probability
requirements.description: One probability course: S&DS 2410 or S&DS 2380.

requirements.name: Data Analysis
requirements.description: One data analysis course: S&DS 3610 or S&DS 2300.

requirements.name: Discrete Mathematics
requirements.description: One discrete mathematics course: AMTH 2440 or CPSC 2020.

requirements.name: Breadth Areas
requirements.description: Three courses drawn from at least three different areas of the item 5 list (optimization; probability and statistics; partial differential equations and analysis; algorithms and numerical methods; graph theory; mathematical economics; engineering; data mining and machine learning; biological modeling and computation; physical sciences; mathematical linguistics and philosophy). The options below are the courses the catalog names; the DUS maintains a longer, changing list, so a course approved by the DUS that is missing here can be added by hand. This app cannot check that the three come from three different areas.

requirements.name: Concentration Courses
requirements.description: Three advanced courses in one field in which mathematics is applied. The standard concentration is three courses from a single item 5 area, at least two of them numbered 3000 or above; any other shape has to be worked out with the DUS. Students doing two majors may overlap two courses with the other major. Because the field is the student's own choice, mark these courses yourself.

requirements.name: Senior Project
requirements.description: Senior thesis research project, AMTH 4910.

AMTH_BS.name: Applied Mathematics, B.S.
AMTH_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics

requirements.name: Computer Programming
requirements.description: Programming is a prerequisite for the major and can be met with either ENAS 1300 or CPSC 1001. It does not count toward the courses required beyond the prerequisites.

requirements.name: Multivariable Calculus
requirements.description: Prerequisite, to be taken before or during sophomore year: MATH 1200 or ENAS 1510, or the equivalent.

requirements.name: Linear Algebra
requirements.description: Prerequisite, to be taken before or during sophomore year: MATH 2220 (cross-listed as AMTH 2220), MATH 2250 or MATH 2260.

requirements.name: Differential Equations
requirements.description: One differential equations course: ENAS 1940 or MATH 2460.

requirements.name: Probability
requirements.description: One probability course: S&DS 2410 or S&DS 2380.

requirements.name: Data Analysis
requirements.description: One data analysis course: S&DS 3610 or S&DS 2300.

requirements.name: Discrete Mathematics
requirements.description: One discrete mathematics course: AMTH 2440 or CPSC 2020.

requirements.name: Breadth Areas
requirements.description: Three courses drawn from at least three different areas of the item 5 list (optimization; probability and statistics; partial differential equations and analysis; algorithms and numerical methods; graph theory; mathematical economics; engineering; data mining and machine learning; biological modeling and computation; physical sciences; mathematical linguistics and philosophy). The options below are the courses the catalog names; the DUS maintains a longer, changing list, so a course approved by the DUS that is missing here can be added by hand. This app cannot check that the three come from three different areas.

requirements.name: Concentration Courses
requirements.description: Three advanced courses in one field in which mathematics is applied. The standard concentration is three courses from a single item 5 area, at least two of them numbered 3000 or above; any other shape has to be worked out with the DUS. Students doing two majors may overlap two courses with the other major. Because the field is the student's own choice, mark these courses yourself.

requirements.name: Vector Analysis

requirements.name: Theory Course

requirements.name: Electives

requirements.name: Senior Requirement

EAST_ASIAN_STUDIES_BA.name: East Asian Studies, B.A.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: East Asian Language L2
requirements.description: Completion of the L2 level of an East Asian language taught at Yale (CHNS 1200, JAPN 1200, or KREN 1200) or the equivalent by placement. The prerequisite is not one of the 13 credits of the major.

requirements.name: East Asian Language Requirement
requirements.description: Six course credits in East Asian language courses beyond the prerequisite, including two credits of advanced (L5) study. Because L3 and L4 terms are 1.5 credits and L5 terms are 1 credit, six credits is normally five courses. With DUS approval, students who have placed out of L5 study at Yale may replace these language credits with content courses on East Asia.

requirements.name: Courses in Country/Area of Focus
requirements.description: Six course credits related to the chosen area of focus (China, Japan, or Korea), of which one is the senior requirement, tracked separately below. The Council on East Asian Studies publishes the list of approved courses, and the DUS approves the course of study. Up to six credits in the major may come from a preapproved study-abroad program.

requirements.name: Course Outside Area of Focus
requirements.description: One course credit on East Asia outside the student's area of focus.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: A major research project using Chinese, Japanese, or Korean language materials. Three routes: a seminar related to the area of focus culminating in a senior thesis (add it by hand), EAST 4900 as a one-term essay, or the two-term EAST 4910 and EAST 4920 (half a credit each, one credit together). The two area-of-focus seminars must be finished first. This course is one of the six area-of-focus credits.

CENG_ES_BS.name: Engineering Sciences (Chemical), B.S.
CENG_ES_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Sciences (Chemical)

requirements.name: Calculus III
requirements.description: ENAS 1510 or MATH 1200.

requirements.name: General Chemistry Sequence
requirements.description: Two terms: CHEM 1610 and 1650, or the advanced sequence CHEM 1630 and 1670 (Advanced University Chemistry I and II, listed in DI's course catalog as CHEM 163 and CHEM 167). Both terms should come from the same sequence.

requirements.name: General Chemistry Laboratory
requirements.description: CHEM 1340L and CHEM 1360L, half a credit each.

requirements.name: Physics Sequence
requirements.description: Two terms of physics: PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010, or the intensive sequence PHYS 2600 and 2610. Both terms should come from the same sequence.

requirements.name: Computing
requirements.description: One of ENAS 1300, CPSC 1001, or CPSC 2000.

requirements.name: Organic Chemistry

requirements.name: Transport Phenomena I
requirements.description: CENG 3140 or MENG 3422.

requirements.name: Engineering Elective
requirements.description: One engineering elective, chosen in consultation with the DUS.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement

URBN.name: Urban Studies, B.A.
URBN.description: Interdisciplinary B.A. focused on the study of cities, the built environment, and urban life, integrating history, design, theory, and methods.

requirements.name: Survey Courses
requirements.description: Three survey courses, at least one of them a URBN course, normally finished by the end of the second year. Further approved surveys are published on Yale Course Search under the attribute YC URBN Survey Course and can be added by hand.

requirements.name: Methods Courses
requirements.description: Three methods courses, one of which must be an Urban Lab (1.5 credits each; see the Urban Lab requirement below). Try to finish two by the end of junior year. Further approved methods courses are published on Yale Course Search under the attribute YC URBN Methods Course.

requirements.name: Urban Lab
requirements.description: One of your three methods courses must be an Urban Lab, each worth 1.5 credits. This row restates that constraint; it is not a fourth methods course. The same courses appear in the School of Architecture as ARCH 3304 and ARCH 3310, and further approved labs are published on Yale Course Search under the attribute YC URBN Urban Lab.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Between four and six electives, depending on the credit value of your other courses: five with the yearlong senior project, six with the one-term seminar, and one fewer in each case if you take two Urban Labs at 1.5 credits. Choose them from the approved list (Yale Course Search attribute YC URBN Elective) or by petition to the DUS.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement – Yearlong Option
requirements.description: Yearlong senior project: URBN 4900, Senior Research Colloquium, in the fall and URBN 4901, Senior Project, in the spring — a paper of at least 7,500 words or an approved project in another medium, advised by a member of the architecture faculty. This is an alternative to the one-term option below; complete one of the two, not both, and mark the other fulfilled by hand.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement – One-Term Option
requirements.description: One advanced seminar numbered between URBN 4000 and URBN 4910, chosen with the DUS, with a final paper of at least 6,000 words on top of the seminar's own work. This route also requires one additional elective (six rather than five). It is an alternative to the yearlong option above; complete one of the two, not both, and mark the other fulfilled by hand. The catalog gives a number range rather than a list, so add your seminar here by hand.

RSEE_RUSSIAN.name: Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies, B.A. - Russian Studies Concentration
RSEE_RUSSIAN.description: Russian Studies Concentration for the B.A. in Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: Second-Year Russian
requirements.description: Completion of second-year Russian (RUSS 1400, RUSS 1420, or RUSS 1450) or the Russian placement exam. The prerequisite is not one of the 12 courses of the major.

requirements.name: Third-Year Russian I
requirements.description: RUSS 1500 (1.5 credits), or an equivalency exam demonstrating Russian proficiency. If proficiency is met without coursework, the total must still reach 12 courses through additional terms.

requirements.name: Third-Year Russian II
requirements.description: RUSS 1510 (1.5 credits), or an equivalency exam demonstrating Russian proficiency. If proficiency is met without coursework, the total must still reach 12 courses through additional terms.

requirements.name: Russian/East European/Eurasian History
requirements.description: Two courses in Russian, East European, or Eurasian history, from any department.

requirements.name: Russian/East European/Eurasian Literature or Culture
requirements.description: One course in Russian, East European, or Eurasian literature or culture, selected in consultation with the DUS.

requirements.name: RSEE-area Social Science
requirements.description: One RSEE-area focused course in the social sciences - anthropology, economics, sociology, political science, global affairs or another social science discipline - with DUS approval.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Five electives, chosen with the DUS, to bring the major to 12 term courses. They may include RUSS 1600 and 1610, a content course taught in Russian at the 1700-1900 level, or courses in other East European or Eurasian languages at the second-year level or above. At most five language courses in total may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: RSEE 4900 or RSEE 4910. Students may enrol in both, but only one counts toward the major.

RSEE_EAST_EUROPEAN.name: Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies, B.A. - East European Studies Concentration
RSEE_EAST_EUROPEAN.description: East European Studies Concentration for the B.A. in Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: First-Year East European/Eurasian Language Sequence
requirements.description: Two terms of a first-year sequence in an East European or Eurasian language, or a placement exam. Yale currently teaches the first year of Czech, Polish, Ukrainian, Bosnian-Croatian-Serbian, and Hungarian; other languages (including Romanian and the Shared Course Initiative languages) also count. The prerequisite is not one of the 11 courses of the major.

requirements.name: Second-Year East European/Eurasian Language I
requirements.description: First term of the second year of the chosen East European or Eurasian language. Part of the four language courses that carry the student to third-year proficiency; an equivalency exam or approved study abroad may substitute.

requirements.name: Second-Year East European/Eurasian Language II
requirements.description: Second term of the second year of the chosen East European or Eurasian language. An equivalency exam or approved study abroad may substitute.

requirements.name: Third-Year East European/Eurasian Language I
requirements.description: First term of the third year of the chosen East European or Eurasian language. Yale teaches advanced Polish, Ukrainian, and Hungarian; for languages where Yale stops at the second year, the level is reached by equivalency exam, the Shared Course Initiative, or study abroad.

requirements.name: Third-Year East European/Eurasian Language II
requirements.description: Second term of the third year of the chosen East European or Eurasian language. Ukrainian is the only one of these languages with a second advanced term at Yale; otherwise the level is reached by equivalency exam, the Shared Course Initiative, or study abroad.

requirements.name: Russian/East European/Eurasian History
requirements.description: Two courses in Russian, East European, or Eurasian history, from any department.

requirements.name: Russian/East European/Eurasian Literature or Culture
requirements.description: One course in Russian, East European, or Eurasian literature or culture, selected in consultation with the DUS.

requirements.name: RSEE-area Social Science
requirements.description: One RSEE-area focused course in the social sciences - anthropology, economics, sociology, political science, global affairs or another social science discipline - with DUS approval.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: The remaining two courses, chosen in consultation with the DUS, to bring the major to 11 term courses.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: RSEE 4900 or RSEE 4910. Students may enrol in both, but only one counts toward the major.

RSEE_EURASIAN.name: Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies, B.A. - Eurasian Studies Concentration
RSEE_EURASIAN.description: Eurasian Studies Concentration for the B.A. in Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies.

requirements.description: Two terms of a first-year sequence in a Eurasian or East European language, or a placement exam. Yale currently teaches the first year of Turkish, Czech, Polish, Ukrainian, Bosnian-Croatian-Serbian, and Hungarian; the Shared Course Initiative languages (Kazakh, Uzbek, Tajik and others) also count. The prerequisite is not one of the 11 courses of the major.

requirements.name: Second-Year Eurasian/East European Language I
requirements.description: First term of the second year of the chosen Eurasian or East European language. Part of the four language courses that carry the student to third-year proficiency; an equivalency exam or approved study abroad may substitute.

requirements.name: Second-Year Eurasian/East European Language II
requirements.description: Second term of the second year of the chosen Eurasian or East European language. An equivalency exam or approved study abroad may substitute.

requirements.name: Third-Year Eurasian/East European Language I
requirements.description: First term of the third year of the chosen Eurasian or East European language. Yale teaches advanced Turkish, Polish, Ukrainian, and Hungarian; for languages where Yale stops at the second year, the level is reached by equivalency exam, the Shared Course Initiative, or study abroad.

requirements.name: Third-Year Eurasian/East European Language II
requirements.description: Second term of the third year of the chosen Eurasian or East European language. Ukrainian is the only one of these languages with a second advanced term at Yale; otherwise the level is reached by equivalency exam, the Shared Course Initiative, or study abroad.

requirements.name: Russian/East European/Eurasian History
requirements.description: Two courses in Russian, East European, or Eurasian history, from any department.

requirements.name: Russian/East European/Eurasian Literature or Culture

requirements.name: Electives

requirements.name: Senior Essay
