FILM_BA.name: Film and Media Studies, B.A.
FILM_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Media Studies

requirements.name: Intro to Film Studies
requirements.description: FILM 1501, Introduction to Film Studies, preferably in the first or second year. It is a prerequisite for most production seminars and many critical studies courses.

requirements.name: Film Analysis
requirements.description: FILM 1601, Introduction to Media, preferably in the first or second year.

requirements.name: Film Theory and Aesthetics
requirements.description: FILM 3201, Close Analysis of Film, preferably in the first or second year.

requirements.name: Upper-level National/World Cinema
requirements.description: One upper-level course in non-American national/world cinema (YC FILM World Cinema attribute).

requirements.name: Upper-level Critical Studies
requirements.description: One upper-level course in critical studies (YC FILM Critical Studies attribute).

requirements.name: Production Course
requirements.description: At least one course in the practice of producing cinematic or digital time-based media (YC FILM Production attribute).

requirements.name: Film and Media Studies Electives
requirements.description: Four electives. Courses in other departments or programs may occasionally be substituted with the permission of the DUS.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement (Essay OR Project)
requirements.description: Two terms of senior work, in one of two forms. Senior essay: a yearlong essay of at least fifty pages (FILM 4910 and 4920), or one senior-level seminar plus one term of FILM 4910 or 4920 (at least thirty-five pages), or two terms of senior-level seminars (usually numbered in the 4000s) with a twenty-five page paper in one of them. Senior production or screenwriting project: two terms of workshops - FILM 4870 and 4880 (screenplay), FILM 4550 and 4560 or FILM 4800 and 4810 (short non-fiction video), FILM 4830 and 4840 or FILM 4800 and 4810 (short fiction video), or FILM 4800 and 4810 (unconventional project) - plus co-enrollment in FILM 4940 (0.5 credit) in the last term for the contextualizing essay. FILM 4940 does not count toward the twelve courses required for the major. A prospectus approved by a faculty adviser is due to the DUS by the end of reading week of junior year.

FILM_BA_INTENSIVE.name: Film and Media Studies, B.A. (Intensive Major)
FILM_BA_INTENSIVE.description: Intensive major: Both senior essay and senior project are required.

requirements.name: Intro to Film Studies
requirements.description: FILM 1501, Introduction to Film Studies, preferably in the first or second year. It is a prerequisite for most production seminars and many critical studies courses.

requirements.name: Film Analysis
requirements.description: FILM 1601, Introduction to Media, preferably in the first or second year.

requirements.name: Film Theory and Aesthetics
requirements.description: FILM 3201, Close Analysis of Film, preferably in the first or second year.

requirements.name: Upper-level National/World Cinema
requirements.description: One upper-level course in non-American national/world cinema (YC FILM World Cinema attribute).

requirements.name: Upper-level Critical Studies
requirements.description: One upper-level course in critical studies (YC FILM Critical Studies attribute).

requirements.name: Production Course
requirements.description: At least one course in the practice of producing cinematic or digital time-based media (YC FILM Production attribute).

requirements.name: Film and Media Studies Electives
requirements.description: Four electives. Courses in other departments or programs may occasionally be substituted with the permission of the DUS.

requirements.name: Senior Essay Requirement
requirements.description: The intensive major requires the senior essay as well as the senior project. Two terms of independent research on a fifty-page essay (FILM 4910 and 4920); alternatively one senior-level seminar plus one term of FILM 4910 or 4920 (at least thirty-five pages), or two terms of senior-level seminars with a twenty-five page paper in one of them.

requirements.name: Senior Project Requirement
requirements.description: Two terms (2 credits) of production or screenwriting workshops for the senior project in production: FILM 4870 and 4880 (screenplay), FILM 4550 and 4560 or FILM 4800 and 4810 (short non-fiction video), FILM 4830 and 4840 or FILM 4800 and 4810 (short fiction video), or FILM 4800 and 4810 (unconventional project). A prospectus form is due by the last day of classes in the spring term of junior year, and approval of the Film and Media Studies Committee is required for the intensive major.

requirements.name: Senior Project Contextualizing Essay
requirements.description: FILM 4940 (0.5 credit), taken in the last term alongside the production or screenwriting workshops, for the roughly fifteen-page contextualizing essay. It does not count toward the twelve courses of the standard major.

ITAL_BA.name: Italian Studies, B.A.
ITAL_BA.description: In-depth linguistic, literary, and cultural study of Italy. Major consists of 11 courses beyond ITAL 1300, with core, distribution, and elective requirements, plus a senior essay in Italian.

requirements.name: Italian Language Prereq
requirements.description: ITAL 1300 (L3) or the equivalent, normally completed by the end of the sophomore year. The prerequisite is not one of the eleven courses for the major.

requirements.name: Foundational Course in Italian Studies
requirements.description: ITAL 1400, Intermediate Italian II, or the equivalent.

requirements.name: Advanced Composition/Conversation
requirements.description: Either ITAL 1500 or ITAL 1510.

requirements.name: Survey of Italian Literature
requirements.description: A survey course on Italian literature: either ITAL 4162 or ITAL 4172.

requirements.name: Dante's Divine Comedy
requirements.description: A course on Dante's Divine Comedy: ITAL 1310 or the equivalent.

requirements.name: Additional Italian Studies Courses (1400+)
requirements.description: 4 additional ITAL courses numbered 1400 or above, for 8 department courses in all. At least 5 of the 8 must be conducted in Italian, and no more than 3 department courses taught in English may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Electives in Other Departments
requirements.description: 2 electives in related areas (other languages and literatures, art history, history, linguistics, philosophy, or media) approved by the DUS. A graduate course in another national literature or in linguistics may substitute for one of them.

requirements.name: Senior Essay in Italian
requirements.description: Departmental essay in Italian written in ITAL 4491, plus meeting with department faculty.

ART_BA.name: Art, B.A.
ART_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Art (Studio Art)

requirements.name: Visual Thinking
requirements.description: ART 1111, Visual Thinking. One of the two mandatory prerequisites; it may not be waived.

requirements.name: Basic Drawing
requirements.description: ART 1514, Basic Drawing. One of the two mandatory prerequisites; it may not be waived.

requirements.name: Introductory Courses (0001-1999, excluding ART 1111 and 1514)
requirements.description: Three more introductory courses numbered 0001-1999, for five prerequisite introductory courses in all. First-Year Seminars count. These may also count as concentration requirements.

requirements.name: Sophomore Review
requirements.description: Favorable faculty review of work done in Yale studio courses, normally in the fourth term. Four of the five introductory prerequisites must be finished and the fifth in progress at the time of the review.

requirements.name: 2000-level or Above Studio Art
requirements.description: Four ART courses numbered 2000 or above. A student who has completed five courses numbered 0001-1999 may count a sixth such course here.

requirements.name: History of Art or DUS-approved Equivalent
requirements.description: Two courses in the history of art, or a DUS-approved equivalent. Students in the filmmaking concentration may substitute two non-production Film and Media Studies courses; other concentrations may do the same only with the permission of the DUS.

requirements.name: Area of Concentration (Graphic Design, Painting/Printmaking, Photography, Sculpture, or Filmmaking)
requirements.description: Five courses from one chosen area of concentration. Suggested courses - graphic design: ART 1732, 2764, 2765, 2766 or 3768, 3769 or 3770, 4768 or 4769; painting/printmaking: ART 1516, 1530, 3531 or 3532, 2545 or 3556, and one of ART 4514, 4532, 3560, 4545, 4533, 4557; photography: ART 1836 and/or 1838, 2837 and/or 2839, 3837 or 3838, and one of ART 3879, 4801, 4803; sculpture: two of ART 1610, 1620, 1621, 1622, 1623 and three of ART 2610, 3646, 3648, 3671, 4646; filmmaking (required, not suggested): ART 1942, 3941, 3942 and ART 4942 or 4943. These five courses overlap with the introductory and 2000-level requirements rather than adding to them.

requirements.name: Junior Seminar
requirements.description: ART 3995, Junior Seminar. Required in every concentration.

requirements.name: Senior Project I
requirements.description: ART 4995, the first term of the two-term senior project.

requirements.name: Senior Project II
requirements.description: ART 4996, the second term of the two-term senior project.

HSHM_BA.name: History of Science, Medicine, and Public Health, B.A.
HSHM_BA.description: The HSHM B.A. is an interdisciplinary major focused on the historical and social dimensions of science, medicine, and public health. Students pursue a concentration and complete a two-term senior project.

requirements.name: HSHM Courses in Concentration
requirements.description: Two of the seven concentration courses must be HSHM courses. Choose a standard concentration (Colonialism, Knowledge, and Power; Environment and Society; Gender, Reproduction, and the Body; Media, Information, and the Public; Medicine and Public Health; Minds and Brains; Science, Technology, and Society) or design your own with the DUS, by the start of junior year.

requirements.name: Seminar in HSHM or HIST (before senior year)
requirements.description: One of the seven concentration courses must be a seminar in HSHM or in History, and at least one of your HSHM/HIST seminars has to be taken before senior year. Listed below are the HSHM seminars; a History seminar counts equally and can be added by hand.

requirements.name: Science Course
requirements.description: One of the seven concentration courses must be a full-credit science course — any Yale course carrying the Sc distributional credit. There are hundreds, so add yours by hand.

requirements.name: Related Electives in Concentration
requirements.description: Three further courses in your concentration, chosen from relevant offerings in any department with your adviser.

requirements.name: Additional HSHM Electives
requirements.description: Three HSHM electives beyond the seven concentration courses. One must be a seminar, and one must come from a concentration other than the one you chose.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: The two-term senior project, HSHM 4900 in the fall and HSHM 4910 in the spring. The Senior Project Workshop, HSHM 4200, is an optional half-credit elective on top of the twelve courses, not a substitute for either term.

EPE_BA.name: Ethics, Politics, and Economics, B.A.
EPE_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Ethics, Politics, and Economics (EP&E)

requirements.name: Introductory: Ethics
requirements.description: PHIL 1175. Two full terms of Directed Studies satisfy this requirement together with Other Perspectives and Political Philosophy.

requirements.name: Introductory: Other Perspectives
requirements.description: One course in Other Perspectives, from disciplines such as Anthropology; Ethnicity, Race, and Migration; History; Sociology; or Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies. Two full terms of Directed Studies also satisfy it. The approved list is published by the EP&E program each year.

requirements.name: Introductory: Political Philosophy
requirements.description: PHIL 1178, PLSC 1327, PLSC 1335 (The Moral Foundations of Politics), or PLSC 1352. Two full terms of Directed Studies also satisfy it.

requirements.name: Introductory: Political Science Intro
requirements.description: One Political Science introductory course: international relations (PLSC 1113), comparative politics (PLSC 1413), or American politics (PLSC 1222).

requirements.name: Introductory: Intro to Macroeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 1111 or 1116.

requirements.name: Introductory: Econometrics
requirements.description: One of ECON 1117, ECON 2123, ECON 2135, GLBL 2121, S&DS 2300, or S&DS 2380.

requirements.name: Introductory: Game Theory
requirements.description: One of EP&E 4220, EP&E 4231, EP&E 4295, EP&E 4297, or ECON 2159. EP&E 4220 and 4231 are not currently listed in the course catalog.

requirements.name: Intermediate Microeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 2121 or ECON 2125.

requirements.name: Core Seminar: EP&E Classics
requirements.description: One course from the EP&E Classics series: EP&E 3212, 3213, 3214, 3215, 3216, or 3217. Only 3212, 3214, and 3217 are currently listed in the course catalog.

requirements.name: Core Seminar: Second Core Area
requirements.description: One approved core course from one of the three core areas (Ethics, Politics, Economics). The approved list is published annually by EP&E and flagged in Yale Course Search as YC EP&E Ethics Core, YC EP&E Politics Core, or YC EP&E Economics Core.

requirements.name: Core Seminar: Third Core Area (Advanced Seminar)
requirements.description: A second approved core course, from a different core area, which must be an advanced seminar anchored in at least two of the three areas (Ethics, Politics, Economics).

requirements.name: Concentration Course 1
requirements.description: First of three courses in the area of concentration you define with the DUS by the end of junior year. At most one of the three may be a lecture course.

requirements.name: Concentration Course 2
requirements.description: Second of three courses in the area of concentration. Seminars from other departments and programs are encouraged.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement (Essay/Concentration Course 3)
requirements.description: Senior essay in the area of concentration, written in EP&E 4491 (one term), EP&E 4492 and 4493 (yearlong), or in a relevant seminar with the instructor's and DUS's approval. It is the third concentration course.

ERM_BA.name: Ethnicity, Race, and Migration, B.A.
ERM_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Ethnicity, Race, and Migration: twelve course credits including the introductory course, the junior seminar, a six-course area of interest, and the senior requirement.

requirements.name: Introductory Course
requirements.description: ER&M 2000, an introduction to the issues and disciplines involved in the study of ethnicity, race, and migration, normally taken in the first or sophomore year.

requirements.name: Junior Seminar
requirements.description: ER&M 3000, the junior-year seminar introducing majors to scholarship in ethnic studies, postcolonial studies, and cultural studies. It may not be taken Credit/D/Fail.

requirements.name: Area of Interest Courses
requirements.description: Six term courses forming an area of interest defined with the DUS, one of which must be a methods course. The senior essay or project does not count here. Advanced work in a language related to the area of interest is advised.

requirements.name: ER&M Content Courses (DUS Approved)
requirements.description: Two additional courses with content related to ethnicity, race, and migration, approved by the DUS. At most two courses counted toward the major may come from other departments.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: Either the yearlong route — the senior colloquium ER&M 4091 in the fall and the senior essay or project seminar ER&M 4092 in the spring — or two upper-level ER&M seminars in either term, writing a 20-25 page final paper in one of them with the instructor's approval. On the two-seminar route, record both seminars here manually. Courses counting toward the senior requirement may not be taken Credit/D/Fail.

MUSI_BA.name: Music, B.A.
MUSI_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Music. Includes music theory, composition, history, technology, and performance across Western, popular, and global traditions.

requirements.name: Group I: Theory & Technology (Intermediate)
requirements.description: Two intermediate Group I courses. Group I is music theory and technology, defined by number: MUSI 2100-2199 and 3100-3199 at the intermediate level. With permission of the DUS, one 1000-level course may replace one intermediate course in this group.

requirements.name: Group I: Theory & Technology (Advanced)
requirements.description: One advanced Group I course, numbered MUSI 4100-4199.

requirements.name: Group II: Composition, Technology & Performance (Intermediate)
requirements.description: Two intermediate Group II courses. Group II is composition, technology and performance, defined by number: MUSI 2200-2299 and 3200-3299 at the intermediate level. Performance lessons (MUSI 3245) sit in this group; up to three credits of lessons may count toward the major. Some chamber-music and lessons courses carry 0.5 credits. With permission of the DUS, one 1000-level course may replace one intermediate course in this group.

requirements.name: Group II: Composition, Technology & Performance (Advanced)
requirements.description: One advanced Group II course, numbered MUSI 4200-4299. Advanced lessons (MUSI 4245, MUSI 4246) sit here; MUSI 4246 requires MUSI 4483 as one of its two corequisites.

requirements.name: Group III: Western Art Music History (Intermediate)
requirements.description: Two intermediate Group III courses. Group III is research- and writing-based study of the Western art-music tradition, defined by number: MUSI 2300-2399 and 3300-3399 at the intermediate level. With permission of the DUS, one 1000-level course may replace one intermediate course in this group.

requirements.name: Group III: Western Art Music History (Advanced)
requirements.description: One advanced Group III course, numbered MUSI 4300-4399.

requirements.name: Group IV: Popular/Global/Non-Western (Intermediate)
requirements.description: Two intermediate Group IV courses. Group IV is research- and writing-based study of popular or vernacular music and music of non-Western traditions, defined by number: MUSI 2400-2499 and 3400-3499 at the intermediate level. With permission of the DUS, one 1000-level course may replace one intermediate course in this group.

requirements.name: Group IV: Popular/Global/Non-Western (Advanced)
requirements.description: One advanced Group IV course, numbered MUSI 4400-4494.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: One term of the senior essay, project, composition, or recital: MUSI 4996, 4997, 4998, or 4999. A completed Senior Project Form is due to the DUS by the end of the course selection period of that term.

MUSI_BA_INTENSIVE.name: Music, B.A. Intensive
MUSI_BA_INTENSIVE.description: Bachelor of Arts in Music (Intensive). The thirteen courses of the standard major plus a second term of the senior project in music research or composition.

requirements.name: Group I: Theory & Technology (Intermediate)
requirements.description: Two intermediate Group I courses. Group I is music theory and technology, defined by number: MUSI 2100-2199 and 3100-3199 at the intermediate level. With permission of the DUS, one 1000-level course may replace one intermediate course in this group.

requirements.name: Group I: Theory & Technology (Advanced)
requirements.description: One advanced Group I course, numbered MUSI 4100-4199.

requirements.name: Group II: Composition, Technology & Performance (Intermediate)
requirements.description: Two intermediate Group II courses. Group II is composition, technology and performance, defined by number: MUSI 2200-2299 and 3200-3299 at the intermediate level. Performance lessons (MUSI 3245) sit in this group; up to three credits of lessons may count toward the major. Some chamber-music and lessons courses carry 0.5 credits. With permission of the DUS, one 1000-level course may replace one intermediate course in this group.

requirements.name: Group II: Composition, Technology & Performance (Advanced)
requirements.description: One advanced Group II course, numbered MUSI 4200-4299. Advanced lessons (MUSI 4245, MUSI 4246) sit here; MUSI 4246 requires MUSI 4483 as one of its two corequisites.

requirements.name: Group III: Western Art Music History (Intermediate)
requirements.description: Two intermediate Group III courses. Group III is research- and writing-based study of the Western art-music tradition, defined by number: MUSI 2300-2399 and 3300-3399 at the intermediate level. With permission of the DUS, one 1000-level course may replace one intermediate course in this group.

requirements.name: Group III: Western Art Music History (Advanced)
requirements.description: One advanced Group III course, numbered MUSI 4300-4399.

requirements.name: Group IV: Popular/Global/Non-Western (Intermediate)
requirements.description: Two intermediate Group IV courses. Group IV is research- and writing-based study of popular or vernacular music and music of non-Western traditions, defined by number: MUSI 2400-2499 and 3400-3499 at the intermediate level. With permission of the DUS, one 1000-level course may replace one intermediate course in this group.

requirements.name: Group IV: Popular/Global/Non-Western (Advanced)
requirements.description: One advanced Group IV course, numbered MUSI 4400-4494.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: First term of the two-term senior project in music research or composition: MUSI 4997, 4998, or 4999, registered in the second-to-last term at Yale. The project proposal must include a plan for progress with a deliverable end-of-term product of roughly the scope of a one-term senior project. The recital option (MUSI 4996) is not available for the intensive major.

requirements.name: Second Senior Project
requirements.description: Second term of registration in the senior project (MUSI 4997, 4998, or 4999), entered after satisfactory completion of the first term. This additional course is supplementary to the thirteen courses of the standard major. DI cannot tell a second term of registration in the same course from the first, so mark this requirement fulfilled by hand.

EALL_CHINESE.name: East Asian Languages and Literatures, B.A. – Chinese Concentration
EALL_CHINESE.description: Focuses on advanced Chinese language and literature, including analysis of texts, theater, film, and culture.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: Advanced Intermediate Chinese
requirements.description: CHNS 1400 or the equivalent, established by the departmental placement exam. The prerequisite is not one of the 11 courses of the major.

requirements.name: Chinese Advanced Modern Sequence
requirements.description: CHNS 1500 and 1510, or equivalents established by placement or approved study abroad.

requirements.name: Chinese Literary Tradition
requirements.description: CHNS 1700, Introduction to Literary Chinese I.

requirements.name: Survey Course in East Asian History and Culture
requirements.description: One survey course in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or East Asian history and culture, preferably taken early. The catalog names no list and surveys are offered in several departments, so add the course by hand.

requirements.name: Literature in Translation
requirements.description: Three literature-in-translation courses taught in English, selected from EALL 2000-3999; at least one must be focused primarily on premodern content. Courses on theater and film may count.

requirements.name: Advanced Courses with Readings in Chinese
requirements.description: Three advanced courses with readings in literary or modern Chinese, Japanese, and/or Korean, beyond CHNS 1500, 1510, and 1700. The menu lists every advanced language course in the three departments because the catalog allows readings in any of the three languages; the DUS confirms which count for the Chinese concentration.

requirements.name: Senior Essay Requirement
requirements.description: A one-term senior essay (EALL 4910) or a yearlong senior essay (EALL 4920 and 4930). The second term of a yearlong essay may not be substituted for any of the 11 required courses, so a yearlong essay means 12 term courses in the major.

EALL_JAPANESE.name: East Asian Languages and Literatures, B.A. – Japanese Concentration
EALL_JAPANESE.description: Focuses on advanced Japanese language and literature, with analysis of texts, theater, film, and culture.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: Advanced Intermediate Japanese
requirements.description: JAPN 1400 or the equivalent, established by the departmental placement exam. The prerequisite is not one of the 11 courses of the major.

requirements.name: Japanese Advanced Modern Sequence
requirements.description: JAPN 1500 and 1510, or equivalents established by placement or approved study abroad.

requirements.name: Japanese Literary Tradition
requirements.description: JAPN 1700, Introduction to Literary Japanese.

requirements.name: Survey Course in East Asian History and Culture
requirements.description: One survey course in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or East Asian history and culture, preferably taken early. The catalog names no list and surveys are offered in several departments, so add the course by hand.

requirements.name: Literature in Translation
requirements.description: Three literature-in-translation courses taught in English, selected from EALL 2000-3999; at least one must be focused primarily on premodern content. Courses on theater and film may count.

requirements.name: Advanced Courses with Readings in Japanese
requirements.description: Three advanced courses with readings in literary or modern Chinese, Japanese, and/or Korean, beyond JAPN 1500, 1510, and 1700. The menu lists every advanced language course in the three departments because the catalog allows readings in any of the three languages; the DUS confirms which count for the Japanese concentration.

requirements.name: Senior Essay Requirement
requirements.description: A one-term senior essay (EALL 4910) or a yearlong senior essay (EALL 4920 and 4930). The second term of a yearlong essay may not be substituted for any of the 11 required courses, so a yearlong essay means 12 term courses in the major.

EALL_KOREAN.name: East Asian Languages and Literatures, B.A. – Korean Concentration
EALL_KOREAN.description: Focuses on advanced Korean language and literature, analysis of texts, film, culture, and media.

requirements.name: Prerequisite: Advanced Intermediate Korean
requirements.description: KREN 1400 or the equivalent, established by the departmental placement exam. The prerequisite is not one of the 11 courses of the major.

requirements.name: Korean Advanced Modern Sequence
requirements.description: KREN 1500 and 1510, or equivalents established by placement or approved study abroad.

requirements.name: Korean Literary Tradition
requirements.description: KREN 1700, Introduction to Hanja.

requirements.name: Survey Course in East Asian History and Culture
requirements.description: One survey course in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or East Asian history and culture, preferably taken early. The catalog names no list and surveys are offered in several departments, so add the course by hand.

requirements.name: Literature in Translation
requirements.description: Three literature-in-translation courses taught in English, selected from EALL 2000-3999; at least one must be focused primarily on premodern content. Courses on theater and film may count.

requirements.name: Advanced Courses with Readings in Korean
requirements.description: Three advanced courses with readings in literary or modern Chinese, Japanese, and/or Korean, beyond KREN 1500, 1510, and 1700. The menu lists every advanced language course in the three departments because the catalog allows readings in any of the three languages; the DUS confirms which count for the Korean concentration.

requirements.name: Senior Essay Requirement
requirements.description: A one-term senior essay (EALL 4910) or a yearlong senior essay (EALL 4920 and 4930). The second term of a yearlong essay may not be substituted for any of the 11 required courses, so a yearlong essay means 12 term courses in the major.

requirements.name: Mathematics Prerequisite
requirements.description: MATH 1200, to be completed before beginning the major. MATH 3020 may be substituted, but only after consulting the Math DUS (MATH 3020 itself requires MATH 2250 and 2550 first). A course used here does not count toward the twelve courses of the major.

requirements.name: Introductory Microeconomics Prerequisite
requirements.description: ECON 1110 or 1115, completed before beginning the major. It may instead be replaced by an extra ECON course numbered above 2000, taken beyond the twelve courses of the major.

requirements.name: Introductory Macroeconomics Prerequisite
requirements.description: ECON 1111 or 1116, completed before beginning the major. It may instead be replaced by an extra ECON course numbered above 2000, taken beyond the twelve courses of the major.

requirements.name: Intermediate Microeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 2125 is preferred; ECON 2121 is also acceptable.

requirements.name: Intermediate Macroeconomics
requirements.description: ECON 2126 is preferred; ECON 2122 is also acceptable.

requirements.name: Introduction to Probability and Statistics
requirements.description: ECON 2135, or S&DS 2410 and S&DS 2420 taken together (the pair counts as one economics course, and neither may be counted alongside ECON 2135).

requirements.name: Econometrics
requirements.description: ECON 2136.

requirements.name: Mathematical Economics: General Equilibrium Theory or Similar
requirements.description: One of ECON 3350 or ECON 4433. A course used here cannot also count toward the senior requirement.

requirements.name: Algorithmic Game Theory or Similar
requirements.description: One of ECON 3351 or ECON 4425. A course used here cannot also count toward the senior requirement.

requirements.name: Additional Economics Course
requirements.description: One more ECON course numbered above 2000, bringing the economics side to seven courses. Waived if the senior requirement is met with an Economics theory seminar instead of MATH 4800/4810.

requirements.name: Linear Algebra or Proof-based Linear Algebra
requirements.description: MATH 2250 or MATH 2260.

requirements.name: Real Analysis
requirements.description: MATH 2550 or MATH 2560.

requirements.name: Seminar in Mathematics or Economic Theory Seminar
requirements.description: MATH 4800 or MATH 4810, or an Economics theory seminar (the YC ECON Theory Seminar attribute in Yale Course Search). If an Economics seminar is used, it counts as the seventh economics course and a third mathematics elective is required instead of the Additional Economics Course.

requirements.name: Additional Advanced Mathematics Courses
requirements.description: Two more MATH courses numbered above 2250, excluding MATH 4700, 2410, and 2420. Graduate MATH courses numbered 5000-5999 may count; 6000 and above may not. Substitutions from other departments are not permitted. A third such course is required if the senior requirement is an Economics theory seminar rather than MATH 4800/4810.

LAST_BA.name: Latin American Studies, B.A.
LAST_BA.description: Interdisciplinary major on Latin American societies and cultures: twelve term courses beyond the prerequisite of Spanish or Portuguese at the L3 level, with a program of study approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Introductory Course
requirements.description: One introductory course approved by the DUS; LAST 1100 and LAST 1200 are the standard choices, and another introduction may be approved instead.

requirements.name: Latin American Content Courses
requirements.description: Seven courses with Latin American content from departmental offerings: 2 in the social sciences (anthropology, economics, or political science), 2 in history, 2 in Spanish American or Brazilian literatures beyond the language prerequisite, and 1 in art, architecture, film and media studies, music, or theater studies. A course outside the program's listings counts if at least a third of its syllabus is on the region and the DUS approves.

requirements.name: Additional Electives
requirements.description: Three additional electives approved by the DUS. Across all twelve courses, three must be seminars or upper-level courses taken in the junior and senior years, and one must be taught in Spanish or Portuguese at the L5 level.

requirements.name: Senior Essay or Project
requirements.description: The senior essay LAST 4491 (a one-term research paper planned with an adviser and second reader) or the senior project LAST 4492 (a project executed under a faculty adviser, with a proposal due by the end of the preceding term, an interim review in week five, and an exhibition of selected work).

JDST_BA.name: Jewish Studies, B.A.
JDST_BA.description: Interdisciplinary study of Jewish history, thought, language, and culture: thirteen term courses — three core courses, the language or literature requirement, three courses in each of two areas of concentration, and the senior essay.

requirements.name: Core Courses
requirements.description: At least three courses, each from a different one of these six categories: Hebrew Bible; ancient Judaism (Second Temple or rabbinic literature); pre-modern Jewish history; modern Jewish history; Jewish thought; a survey course in Hebrew or Jewish literature. The catalog names the categories rather than specific courses, so choose them with the DUS and record them here.

requirements.name: Hebrew Language or Literature
requirements.description: HEBR 1100 and HEBR 1200, or two courses in Hebrew literature in translation. Up to three Hebrew or Yiddish language courses may be counted toward the major.

requirements.name: Focus Area I
requirements.description: Three courses in the first area of concentration — ancient Israel/Hebrew Bible; Judaism and Jewish history of the Second Temple and rabbinic periods; Jewish history and culture in the medieval and early modern periods; modern Jewish history and culture; Jewish/Hebrew literature (which requires study of literature in Hebrew or Yiddish); Jewish thought; or a self-designed area approved by the DUS. The three are expected to include one introductory course and one seminar.

requirements.name: Focus Area II
requirements.description: Three courses in the second area of concentration, again including one introductory course and one seminar. One relevant course should be outside the Jewish Studies program — the wider historical, literary, or philosophical context for a period concentration, or the theory or practice of literature for a literature concentration.

requirements.name: Senior Essay Requirement
requirements.description: Either the two-term senior essay JDST 4491 and JDST 4492, related to both areas of concentration, or a one-term senior essay (JDST 4491 or JDST 4492) related to one area plus an additional seminar related to the other. On the one-term path, record the additional seminar here manually.

PHYS_GEOSCI_BS.name: Physics and Geosciences, B.S.
PHYS_GEOSCI_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Physics and Geosciences

requirements.name: Math through Calc III
requirements.description: MATH 1200 or an equivalent multivariable calculus course such as ENAS 1510.

requirements.name: Introductory Physics Sequence
requirements.description: Two courses: one complete lecture sequence, PHYS 1700 and 1710 or above, so PHYS 1700 and 1710, or PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010, or PHYS 2600 and 2610. Both halves must come from the same sequence, and each sequence has its own math corequisites.

requirements.name: Introductory Physics Lab
requirements.description: PHYS 2050L, worth half a credit.

requirements.name: Differential Equations
requirements.description: One course in ordinary differential equations: ENAS 1940, MATH 2460 or PHYS 4000.

requirements.name: Advanced Intro Physics Lab
requirements.description: PHYS 2060L, worth half a credit.

requirements.name: Physics Core Sequence
requirements.description: One complete advanced physics sequence: either the two-term PHYS 4010 and 4020, or the three-term PHYS 4100, PHYS 4300 and PHYS 4500. Students taking the three-term sequence take one course more than the two counted here.

requirements.name: Quantum Mechanics
requirements.description: One term of quantum mechanics: PHYS 4390 or PHYS 4400.

requirements.name: Advanced PHYS Elective
requirements.description: One elective numbered PHYS 3000 or above. A relevant course in a related department may be substituted with the permission of the Physics DUS. No elective may count toward more than one requirement of the major.

requirements.name: Introductory EPS Course (with lab)
requirements.description: One introductory Earth and Planetary Sciences course numbered EPS 1000-1400, taken with its accompanying laboratory where one exists (EPS 1110L goes with EPS 1100, EPS 1260L with EPS 1250). The lab adds half a credit, which is why the major comes to 13 credits beyond the prerequisites rather than 12.5 for students whose introductory course has one.

requirements.name: EPS Upper-Level Elective
requirements.description: One Earth and Planetary Sciences elective numbered EPS 2000 or above. A relevant course in a related department may be substituted with the permission of the Earth and Planetary Sciences DUS.

requirements.name: EPS Advanced Track Courses
requirements.description: Four advanced Earth and Planetary Sciences electives from one track, either Atmosphere, Ocean, and Climate or Solid Earth Science. Relevant courses in related departments may be substituted with the permission of the Earth and Planetary Sciences DUS.

requirements.name: Senior Project
requirements.description: A two-term senior project on a topic acceptable to both departments, taken either as PHYS 4710 and 4720 or as EPS 4900 and EPS 4910 (both terms from the same department). Students must also present an oral report on the project to each department.

ARCH_CONCEN_DESIGN.name: Architecture, B.A. - Design Concentration
ARCH_CONCEN_DESIGN.description: Design Concentration for the B.A. in Architecture

requirements.name: Introduction to Architecture
requirements.description: ARCH 1001. One of the three prerequisites, to be taken by the end of sophomore year.

requirements.name: Scales of Design
requirements.description: ARCH 2000. One of the three prerequisites, to be taken by the end of sophomore year.

requirements.name: Architecture Topics
requirements.description: The third prerequisite: ARCH 2600, American Architecture and Urbanism, or ARCH 2601, Introduction to Urban Design.

requirements.name: Methods and Form I
requirements.description: ARCH 3000, taken in the junior year after acceptance into the major. This studio carries 1.5 credits.

requirements.name: Methods and Form II
requirements.description: ARCH 3001, taken in the junior year. This studio carries 1.5 credits.

requirements.name: History of Architecture to 1750
requirements.description: ARCH 2001, Architecture Before Modernity, one of the two history of architecture surveys, to be completed by the end of junior year.

requirements.name: Modern Architecture
requirements.description: ARCH 2003, Modern Architecture in a Global Context, 1750-present, the second history of architecture survey, to be completed by the end of junior year.

requirements.name: History & Theory of Architecture and the City Elective
requirements.description: One elective in history and theory of architecture and the city (the YC ARCH History & Theory attribute in Yale Course Search): Architecture courses and relevant courses in History of Art and related fields, approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Urbanism and Landscape Elective
requirements.description: One elective in urbanism and landscape (the YC ARCH Urbanism & Landscape attribute): Architecture courses and other relevant courses in American Studies; Ethics, Politics, and Economics; Environmental Studies; or Political Science, approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Materials and Design Elective
requirements.description: One elective in materials and design (the YC ARCH Materials & Design attribute): Architecture courses and ART courses in drawing, painting, sculpture, or graphic design, or any other relevant course approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Structures and Computation Elective
requirements.description: One elective in structures and computation: ARCH 1400, an approved calculus course such as MATH 1120, MATH 1150 or MATH 1200, a physics course such as PHYS 1800 or PHYS 2000, or another relevant course approved by the DUS. Elementary calculus is strongly recommended as preparation for graduate study in architecture.

requirements.name: Senior Studio I
requirements.description: ARCH 4000, taken in the fall term of senior year. This studio carries 1.5 credits.

requirements.name: Senior Studio II
requirements.description: ARCH 4001, taken in the spring term of senior year. This studio carries 1.5 credits. All seniors also submit a portfolio of design work to the DUS by the end of the spring term.

ARCH_CONCEN_HIST.name: Architecture, B.A. - History, Theory, Criticism, and Urbanism Concentration
ARCH_CONCEN_HIST.description: History, Theory, Criticism of Architecture, and Urbanism Concentration for the B.A. in Architecture

requirements.name: Introduction to Architecture
requirements.description: ARCH 1001. One of the three prerequisites, to be taken by the end of sophomore year.

requirements.name: Scales of Design
requirements.description: ARCH 2000. One of the three prerequisites, to be taken by the end of sophomore year.

requirements.name: Architecture Topics
requirements.description: The third prerequisite: ARCH 2600, American Architecture and Urbanism, or ARCH 2601, Introduction to Urban Design.

requirements.name: Methods and Form I
requirements.description: ARCH 3000, taken in the fall term of junior year. This studio carries 1.5 credits.

requirements.name: Urban Lab
requirements.description: A second design studio or urban laboratory taken in the spring term of junior year, or an elective approved by the DUS. The catalog names ARCH 3305 and ARCH 3309 as examples; the studios and urban labs currently in the course catalog are ARCH 3304, ARCH 3310 and the design studio ARCH 3001. These carry 1.5 credits.

requirements.name: History of Architecture to 1750
requirements.description: ARCH 2001, Architecture Before Modernity, one of the two history of architecture surveys, to be completed by the end of junior year.

requirements.name: Modern Architecture
requirements.description: ARCH 2003, Modern Architecture in a Global Context, 1750-present, the second history of architecture survey, to be completed by the end of junior year.

requirements.name: History & Theory of Architecture and the City Electives
requirements.description: Four electives in history and theory of architecture and the city (the YC ARCH History & Theory attribute in Yale Course Search): Architecture courses and relevant courses in History of Art and related fields, all approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Other elective
requirements.description: 1 elective in urbanism and landscape, materials and design, or structures and computation or other relevant course approved by the DUS

requirements.name: Senior Research Colloquium
requirements.description: ARCH 4900, taken in the fall term of senior year.

requirements.name: Senior Project
requirements.description: ARCH 4901, taken in the spring term of senior year; the senior essay or project is due in the DUS office by early April. All seniors also submit a portfolio of design work, including a copy of the senior essay.

SAST.name: South Asian Studies
SAST.description: Second major only. Focuses on history, culture, and languages of South Asia, including both premodern and modern perspectives, and language study through advanced (L5) level.

requirements.name: Premodern South Asia Courses
requirements.description: Two of the seven South Asian Studies courses must address premodern South Asia. The courses that qualify are published as a course attribute by the program rather than listed in the catalog, so add them by hand.

requirements.name: South Asian Studies Seminars
requirements.description: Two of the seven South Asian Studies courses should be seminars. The catalog names no list, so add them by hand.

requirements.name: South Asian Studies Electives
requirements.description: The remaining three of the seven term courses in South Asian Studies numbered 2000 or above. With DUS approval one relevant course from another department or program may count, as may up to three credits of approved study abroad. If the language requirement is met by an L5 exam rather than coursework, an eighth term course is required.

requirements.name: South Asian Language L5
requirements.description: One South Asian language studied at the advanced (L5) level. Yale offers L5 instruction in Hindi (HNDI 1500) and Sanskrit (SKRT 1500, SKRT 1600); Telugu currently stops at L4. Proficiency in another South Asian language can be shown by testing, and the DUS may approve substituting another appropriate language such as Persian or Arabic.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: SAST 4910, a one-credit one-term senior essay, or a senior essay written in a seminar with DUS approval. The essay runs to 8,000-10,000 words and the plan must be approved by the DUS early in the senior year.

MATH_PHYS_BS.name: Mathematics & Physics, B.S.
MATH_PHYS_BS.description: Interdisciplinary major integrating advanced mathematics and physics. Focuses on the synergy between the two fields and prepares students for graduate work or technical careers.

requirements.name: Prereq: Multivariable Calculus
requirements.description: MATH 1200, or MATH 3020 as a substitute. MATH 3020 requires MATH 2250 and MATH 2550 first, and if it is used here it cannot also count toward the six mathematics courses. Students without prior multivariable calculus must consult the Mathematics DUS before choosing MATH 3020.

requirements.name: Prereq: Introductory Physics Sequence
requirements.description: Two courses: one complete introductory lecture sequence numbered PHYS 1800, 1810 or above, so PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010, or PHYS 2600 and 2610. Both halves must come from the same sequence. Students who took PHYS 1700 and 1710 may enter the major with the permission of the Physics DUS.

requirements.name: Prereq: Physics Lab
requirements.description: PHYS 2050L. Students who took the PHYS 1650L and 1660L sequence instead may enter the major with the permission of the Physics DUS. Each of these labs is worth half a credit.

requirements.name: Mathematics Courses
requirements.description: Six mathematics courses numbered MATH 2220-4690. A course from another department counts only if it carries an undergraduate MATH number. Graduate mathematics courses numbered 5000-5999 may be used as electives; 6000 and above may not count toward the major.

requirements.name: Physics Lab: Advanced
requirements.description: PHYS 2060L, worth half a credit.

requirements.name: Advanced Physics Courses
requirements.description: Five advanced physics courses above the introductory level, chosen in consultation with the adviser for the major. With the senior project these make up the six advanced physics courses the catalog requires.

requirements.name: Math or Physics Electives
requirements.description: Two further courses in either mathematics (MATH 2220-4690, or graduate MATH 5000-5999) or physics above the introductory level.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: A senior project in PHYS 4710 or PHYS 4720 on a topic acceptable to both the Physics and the Mathematics departments. It counts as one of the six advanced physics courses.

requirements.name: Introductory Sociology
requirements.description: One introductory Sociology course at the 1000 level (e.g., SOCY 1001, SOCY 1003, SOCY 1012). No more than two introductory courses from any one department may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Sociological Theory I
requirements.description: SOCY 2001, Foundations of Modern Social Theory.

requirements.name: Sociological Theory II
requirements.description: SOCY 2002, Topics in Contemporary Social Theory.

requirements.name: Research Design
requirements.description: SOCY 2100, usually completed in the spring of junior year.

requirements.name: Sociological Methods
requirements.description: One course in a social science methodology, for example S&DS 1000, S&DS 1100, S&DS 3630, GLBL 2122, SOCY 2103, or AMST 3304. Other courses carrying the department's methods attribute also count.

requirements.name: Sociology Electives
requirements.description: Six Sociology electives at the 2000 or 3000 level. One may be a 1000-level introductory course. Courses taken elsewhere or abroad may count with DUS approval, and no more than two Credit/D/Fail courses may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: SOCY 4100, the one-term senior essay for non-intensive majors, written in the senior year.

requirements.name: Advanced Sociology Seminar
requirements.description: One additional 3000-level Sociology seminar (SOCY 3000-3999, e.g., SOCY 3741 or SOCY 3401), taken as the second half of the non-intensive senior requirement.

SOCY_INTENSIVE.name: Sociology, B.A. - Intensive Major
SOCY_INTENSIVE.description: Intensive Major in Sociology. Same as standard or any concentration, but the senior requirement is a two-term independent research project.

requirements.name: Standard Major or Concentration Coursework
requirements.description: The eleven non-senior courses of the standard major or of any concentration. For the standard major that is one 1000-level intro course, SOCY 2001, SOCY 2002, SOCY 2100, one sociological methods course, and six Sociology electives.

requirements.name: Intensive Senior Essay I
requirements.description: SOCY 4200, first term of the yearlong senior essay and colloquium for intensive majors.

requirements.name: Intensive Senior Essay II
requirements.description: SOCY 4201, second term of the yearlong senior essay and colloquium. Only intensive majors are eligible for Distinction in the Major.

SOCY_CONC_ECONOMY.name: Sociology, B.A. - Economy and Society Concentration
SOCY_CONC_ECONOMY.description: Concentration in Economy and Society within the Sociology major.

requirements.name: Introductory Sociology
requirements.description: One introductory Sociology course at the 1000 level (e.g., SOCY 1001, SOCY 1003, SOCY 1012).

requirements.name: Sociological Theory
requirements.description: SOCY 2001 or SOCY 2002.

requirements.name: Research Design
requirements.description: SOCY 2100, usually completed in the spring of junior year.

requirements.name: Microeconomics
requirements.description: One intermediate or advanced microeconomics course, such as ECON 2121 or ECON 2125, or another course approved by the DUS. It counts toward the four courses allowed from outside the Sociology department.

requirements.name: Sociological Methods
requirements.description: One course in social science methodology, for example S&DS 1000, S&DS 1100, S&DS 1600, S&DS 2300, S&DS 3630, GLBL 2122, SOCY 2103, or AMST 3304.

requirements.name: Inequality or Economic Sociology (Intermediate/Advanced)
requirements.description: Two intermediate or advanced courses on inequality or economic sociology, for example SOCY 2800, SOCY 3814, or SOCY 3821, or another course approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Economy and Society Electives
requirements.description: Four electives relevant to economic processes and their social dimension. Together with the microeconomics course, up to four of the major's courses may come from outside the Sociology department with DUS approval.

requirements.name: Senior Essay (Economy/Society)
requirements.description: The senior essay, integrating research on markets, businesses, economic behavior, or inequality: SOCY 4100 for non-intensive majors, or SOCY 4200 and 4201 for intensive majors.

requirements.name: Advanced Sociology Seminar
requirements.description: One 3000-level Sociology seminar (SOCY 3000-3999, e.g., SOCY 3741 or SOCY 3401), the second course of the non-intensive senior requirement.

SOCY_CONC_HEALTH.name: Sociology, B.A. - Health and Society Concentration
SOCY_CONC_HEALTH.description: Concentration in Health and Society within the Sociology major.

requirements.name: Gateway Course
requirements.description: SOCY 1600 or SOCY 1601, the gateway courses for the concentration, or a comparable course approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Sociological Theory
requirements.description: SOCY 2001 or SOCY 2002.

requirements.name: Research Design
requirements.description: SOCY 2100, usually completed in the spring of junior year.

requirements.name: Sociological Methods
requirements.description: One course in a social science methodology, for example S&DS 1000, S&DS 1100, or S&DS 3630.

requirements.name: Intermediate/Advanced Health/Society Seminar
requirements.description: Two intermediate or advanced Sociology seminars relevant to health and society.

requirements.name: Health and Society Electives

requirements.name: Related Field Elective

requirements.name: Senior Tutorial

CLSS_ANC_MOD_GREEK.description: Bachelor of Arts in Ancient and Modern Greek

requirements.description: Four ancient Greek courses numbered 3000 or above, one of which should be GREK 4995.

requirements.name: Greek/Roman History & Literature

AFAM.name: Black Studies, B.A.
AFAM.description: Bachelor of Arts in Black Studies (formerly African American Studies): twelve term courses, seven core and five in a student-designed area of focus.

requirements.name: Foundations of African American Studies I
requirements.description: BLST 1160, The Making of the Black Atlantic, 1400-1900 (earlier titled History of Atlantic Slavery, and cross-listed as AMST 1160 and HIST 1784). The two history-sequence courses may be taken in either order.

requirements.name: Foundations of African American Studies II
requirements.description: BLST 1162, African American History from Emancipation to the Present (cross-listed as AMST 1162 and HIST 1187). The two history-sequence courses may be taken in either order.

requirements.name: African American Literature (HU)
requirements.description: One Black Studies literature course with the HU designation, approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: African American Studies (SO)
requirements.description: One Black Studies course with the SO designation, approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Junior Seminar
requirements.description: The junior seminar, BLST 4310 (Interdisciplinary Approaches to African American Studies), taken in the junior year.

requirements.name: Senior Colloquium
requirements.description: BLST 4380, the senior colloquium, where the prospectus, bibliography, and first twenty pages of the senior essay are written. Listed as AFAM 4380 before the department was renamed.

requirements.name: Senior Essay
requirements.description: BLST 4391, the senior essay, written after the colloquium under a faculty adviser in the area of focus. Listed as AFAM 4391 before the department was renamed.

requirements.name: Focus Area Electives
requirements.description: Five interrelated courses in an area of focus the student designs with the DUS, in a discipline (political science, art history, economics, sociology, American studies, history, English) or as an interdisciplinary theme. None of the seven core courses may count here.

LING_BA.name: Linguistics, B.A.
LING_BA.description: Study of the structure, use, and analysis of human language across subfields. Requires breadth across linguistic subfields, depth in one area, electives, research methods, and a senior essay.

requirements.name: Breadth Requirement
requirements.description: Five courses. Four must come from LING 1179, LING 2120, LING 2200, LING 2270, LING 2320, LING 2530, LING 2630, LING 2750, LING 2790, and LING 3610. The fifth is either another course from that list or a course covering several subfields, such as LING 1100 or LING 1160. Other courses may be substituted with DUS approval.

requirements.name: Depth Requirement
requirements.description: Two courses beyond the introductory level in one of the eight areas of linguistics: historical, computational, phonetics, phonology, syntax, semantics, morphology, or language and mind/brain.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Three additional courses relating to linguistics, at least one at the 2000 level or above. With DUS approval they may come from related programs such as Anthropology, Classics, Cognitive Science, Computer Science, English, Philosophy, Psychology, or foreign languages; no more than two foreign language courses may count without specific DUS approval.

requirements.name: Research Methods in Linguistics
requirements.description: LING 4900, normally taken in the fall term of senior year (fall of junior year for December graduates). It prepares students for the senior essay.

requirements.name: The Senior Essay
requirements.description: LING 4910, written in the final spring term alongside a research colloquium.

MENG.name: Mechanical Engineering (ABET), B.S.
MENG.description: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering (ABET)

requirements.name: Calculus III
requirements.description: ENAS 1510 or MATH 1200, or the equivalent.

requirements.name: Physics Sequence
requirements.description: Two physics lectures: one from PHYS 1800, 2000, or 2600, and one from PHYS 1810, 2010, or 2610, or the equivalents. The two should come from the same sequence.

requirements.name: Physics Labs
requirements.description: Two laboratories (half a credit each): one from PHYS 1650L or PHYS 2050L, and one from PHYS 1660L or PHYS 2060L, or the equivalents.

requirements.name: Introductory Chemistry
requirements.description: One 1-credit chemistry lecture numbered CHEM 1610 or higher, or the equivalent. Waived for a Chemistry AP score of 4 or 5, or an IB Higher or Standard level score of 6 or 7.

requirements.name: Linear Algebra
requirements.description: MATH 2220 or MATH 2250.

requirements.name: Technical Electives
requirements.description: Three technical electives chosen in consultation with the DUS; at most one may be MENG 4991 or MENG 4992. Frequently approved mechanical engineering courses are listed here, and other DUS-approved courses count as well.

requirements.name: Senior Design I
requirements.description: MENG 4137L, taken in the senior year.

requirements.name: Senior Design II
requirements.description: MENG 4138L, a half-credit course taken in the senior year.

MENG_ENGS.name: Engineering Sciences (Mechanical), B.S.
MENG_ENGS.description: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Sciences (Mechanical)

requirements.name: Calc III (Multivar)
requirements.description: ENAS 1510 or MATH 1200, or the equivalent.

requirements.name: Physics Sequence
requirements.description: Two physics lectures: one from PHYS 1800, 2000, or 2600, and one from PHYS 1810, 2010, or 2610, or the equivalents. The two should come from the same sequence.

requirements.name: Physics Labs
requirements.description: Two laboratories: one from PHYS 1650L or PHYS 2050L (half a credit each), and one from PHYS 1660L, PHYS 2060L (half a credit each) or MENG 2616L (1 credit).

requirements.name: MENG Electives
requirements.description: Eleven approved engineering courses chosen with the DUS, forming a coherent program. At most one may be a Special Projects course (MENG 4991 or 4992), counting that one only if it is not used for the senior project.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: A senior project taken in the senior year: MENG 4154, MENG 4991, MENG 4992, or another upper-level design course chosen in consultation with the DUS.

HIST_CONCEN_GLOBAL.name: History, B.A. - Global Concentration
HIST_CONCEN_GLOBAL.description: Global Concentration for the B.A. in History. Students must complete broad regional requirements across five world regions, two preindustrial courses, and two seminars, for a total of 12 credits (including prereqs and senior req).

requirements.name: Prerequisite Courses
requirements.description: Two course credits in History before declaring. They count toward the twelve credits of the major and may also fill region, preindustrial, or seminar requirements. Directed Studies history and philosophy courses count automatically.

requirements.name: Regional Distribution
requirements.description: One course credit in five of the six regions: Africa (Sub-Saharan), Asia, Europe, Latin America, Middle East/North Africa, and United States/Canada. A course's region is shown by the second digit of its number.

requirements.name: Preindustrial History Courses
requirements.description: Two course credits covering material before the mid-19th century (and no later than 1900). The same course may count here and toward a region or seminar requirement.

requirements.name: Departmental Seminars
requirements.description: Two 3000-level departmental seminars. Residential College Seminars, study abroad courses, 2000-level seminars, and courses in other departments do not count here, though they can satisfy other requirements.

requirements.name: Additional History Courses
requirements.description: Further history course credits to reach twelve in all. Up to two may be courses taught outside the department with DUS approval (those may not count as departmental seminars or toward the senior requirement). The second term of a two-term senior essay counts here.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: A two-term senior essay or approved alternative project (HIST 4995 and HIST 4996, two credits, and the only route to Distinction in the Major), or a one-term senior essay (HIST 4997, one credit, with one additional full-credit course to reach twelve).

HIST_CONCEN_SPECIALIST.name: History, B.A. - Specialist Concentration
HIST_CONCEN_SPECIALIST.description: Specialist Concentration for the B.A. in History. Students focus on a region or thematic pathway, with supporting breadth and seminar requirements, for a total of 12 credits (including prereqs and senior req).

requirements.name: Prerequisite Courses
requirements.description: Two course credits in History before declaring. They count toward the twelve credits of the major and may also fill specialization, region, preindustrial, or seminar requirements. Directed Studies history and philosophy courses count automatically.

requirements.name: Specialist Field Courses
requirements.description: At least five, and up to eight, course credits in one geographic region or thematic pathway: cultural history; empires and colonialism; environmental history; ideas and intellectuals; international and diplomatic history; politics, law, and government; race, gender, and sexuality; religion in context; science, technology, and medicine; social change and social movements; war and society; the world economy. A student may also design a specialization with a faculty adviser and the DUS.

requirements.name: Outside Specialist Field
requirements.description: At least two course credits outside the chosen region or pathway.

requirements.name: Regional Breadth
requirements.description: Overall coursework must cover at least three of the six geographic regions. The same courses may count toward the specialization and the outside requirement.

requirements.name: Preindustrial History Courses
requirements.description: Two course credits covering material before the mid-19th century (and no later than 1900). The same course may count here and toward a region, pathway, or seminar requirement.

requirements.name: Departmental Seminars
requirements.description: Two 3000-level departmental seminars. Residential College Seminars, study abroad courses, 2000-level seminars, and courses in other departments do not count here, though they can satisfy other requirements.

requirements.name: Additional History Courses
requirements.description: Further history course credits to reach twelve in all; these may extend the specialization to as many as eight credits. Up to two may be courses taught outside the department with DUS approval (those may not count as departmental seminars or toward the senior requirement). The second term of a two-term senior essay counts here.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: A two-term senior essay or approved alternative project (HIST 4995 and HIST 4996, two credits, and the only route to Distinction in the Major), or a one-term senior essay (HIST 4997, one credit, with one additional full-credit course to reach twelve).

requirements.name: Statistics or Psychology Prerequisite

requirements.name: Neuroscience Foundations

requirements.name: Molecular/Cellular/Biological Core

requirements.name: Quantitative Core

requirements.name: Computational Core

HUMS_BA.name: Humanities, B.A.
HUMS_BA.description: Integrates literature, arts, science in the humanities, and intellectual history. Six core seminars, broad distribution, area of focus, and a senior essay.

requirements.name: Core Modernities Seminars
requirements.description: Two core "Modernities" seminars. Topics and instructors rotate each year, so these are identified by the Humanities major attribute in the course listings rather than by fixed course numbers. No more than four of the six core courses may concern one world-historical tradition.

requirements.name: Core Interpretations Seminars
requirements.description: Two core "Interpretations" seminars, each spending a term on a single work or small corpus. Topics and instructors rotate each year, so these are identified by the Humanities major attribute in the course listings rather than by fixed course numbers.

requirements.name: Core Traditions Lectures/Seminars
requirements.description: Two core "Traditions" lectures or seminars surveying foundational works, covering at least two different cultural traditions and including at least one course on classical Western European texts. Offerings rotate, so they carry the Humanities major attribute rather than fixed course numbers.

requirements.name: Literature Requirement
requirements.description: 1 course in literature (may be from any department; DUS approval required).

requirements.name: Visual, Musical, or Dramatic Arts Requirement
requirements.description: 1 course in the visual, musical, or dramatic arts (any department; DUS approval required).

requirements.name: Science in the Humanities Requirement
requirements.description: 1 course in science in the humanities (any department; DUS approval required).

requirements.name: Intellectual History and Historical Analysis Requirement
requirements.description: 1 course in intellectual history and historical analysis (any department; DUS approval required). A Franke Seminar may count for one of the four area requirements.

requirements.name: Electives in Area of Focus
requirements.description: 3 electives to complement area of focus (approved by DUS).

requirements.name: Intellectual Journal
