ENVE_BA.name: Engineering Sciences (Environmental), B.A.
ENVE_BA.description: B.A. degree in Engineering Sciences (Environmental) at Yale College

requirements.name: Calculus I & II
requirements.description: MATH 1120 and MATH 1150.

requirements.name: General Chemistry (2 terms)
requirements.description: A two-term lecture sequence in chemistry: CHEM 1610 and 1650, or the advanced sequence CHEM 1630 and 1670 (listed in DI's course catalog as CHEM 163 and CHEM 167). Both terms should come from the same sequence.

requirements.name: General Physics (Life Science sequence)
requirements.description: PHYS 1700 and PHYS 1710.

requirements.name: Air Pollution or Water-Energy Nexus
requirements.description: ENVE 3730 or ENVE 3770.

requirements.name: ENVE Electives (DUS approved)
requirements.description: Five electives chosen in consultation with the DUS. They may build toward an optional area of emphasis: Climate and Energy; Environmental Science and Technology; Sustainability and Policy; or self-designed.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: Pass ENVE 4160 or ENVE 4900 in the senior year.

ENVE_BS.name: Environmental Engineering, B.S.
ENVE_BS.description: B.S. degree in Environmental Engineering at Yale College

requirements.name: Calculus I & II
requirements.description: MATH 1120 and MATH 1150.

requirements.name: Multivariable Calculus
requirements.description: MATH 1200 or ENAS 1510.

requirements.name: Ordinary Differential Equations
requirements.description: ENAS 1940, Differential Equations for Engineers.

requirements.name: Statistics / Data Science
requirements.description: ENAS 1300 or S&DS 2300.

requirements.name: General Chemistry (2 terms with lab)
requirements.description: A two-term lecture sequence in chemistry: CHEM 1610 and 1650, or the advanced sequence CHEM 1630 and 1670 (listed in DI's course catalog as CHEM 163 and CHEM 167). Both terms should come from the same sequence, and the corresponding labs are required as well.

requirements.name: Labs for Gen Chem
requirements.description: Both accompanying general chemistry labs, CHEM 1340L and CHEM 1360L, half a credit each.

requirements.name: General Physics Sequence
requirements.description: PHYS 1800 and PHYS 1810.

requirements.name: Introductory Biology
requirements.description: BIOL 1010 and 1020, or BIOL 1030 and 1040 (half a credit each). Both terms should come from the same pair.

requirements.name: Thermodynamics
requirements.description: CENG 3000 or MENG 2511.

requirements.name: Transport Phenomena / Advanced Water
requirements.description: ENVE 3140 (Transport Phenomena I) or ENVE 4480, Environmental Transport Processes, which DI's course catalog lists as ENVE 448.

requirements.name: Environmental Organic Chemistry
requirements.description: ENVE 4380 (Environmental Organic Chemistry) or ENVE 4400 (Aquatic Chemistry).

requirements.name: Physical/Chemical Processes
requirements.description: ENVE 4420, Environmental Physicochemical Processes.

requirements.name: ENVE Electives (DUS approved)
requirements.description: Four electives approved by the DUS, at least three of which must be technical electives. They may build toward an optional area of emphasis: Climate and Energy; Environmental Science and Technology; Sustainability and Policy; or self-designed.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: Pass ENVE 4160 or ENVE 4900 in the senior year.

PHIL_BA.name: Philosophy, B.A.
PHIL_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy (Standard Major)

requirements.name: Prerequisite Introductory or Intermediate Philosophy Courses
requirements.description: Two introductory or intermediate philosophy courses. These count inside the twelve courses of the major.

requirements.name: History of Philosophy
requirements.description: Three courses in the history of philosophy group, which must include PHIL 1125 and PHIL 1126 (DRST 0003 and DRST 0004 may substitute for them). The third may be any course listed in the history of philosophy group in Yale Course Search, so add it here manually.

requirements.name: Metaphysics and Epistemology
requirements.description: Two courses listed in the metaphysics and epistemology group in Yale Course Search. No course may count toward two group requirements.

requirements.name: Ethics and Value Theory
requirements.description: Two courses listed in the ethics and value theory group in Yale Course Search. No course may count toward two group requirements.

requirements.name: Logic
requirements.description: One logic course, preferably by the fall of junior year. PHIL 1115, First-Order Logic, is the usual choice.

requirements.name: Philosophy Seminars at 3000-level or above
requirements.description: Two advanced philosophy seminars numbered 3000 or above. Either or both may also count toward one of the group requirements above, so these two need not be extra courses.

requirements.name: Elective Philosophy Courses
requirements.description: One further course to reach twelve in the major. Any philosophy course counts; with DUS approval up to two courses from other departments may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: Normally a third philosophy seminar taken with extra work agreed with the instructor; alternatively a one- or two-term independent project (PHIL 4490, PHIL 4491) proposed to the DUS the term before. Add the seminar manually if you take that route.

PHIL_PSYCH_BA.name: Philosophy, B.A. (Psychology Concentration)
PHIL_PSYCH_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy with a Concentration in Psychology

requirements.name: Prerequisite Philosophy or Psychology Courses
requirements.description: Two introductory or intermediate courses in philosophy or psychology. These count inside the twelve courses of the concentration.

requirements.name: Introductory Psychology
requirements.description: PSYC 1100, Introduction to Psychology, or its equivalent. One of the five psychology courses.

requirements.name: Psychology Courses
requirements.description: Four further psychology courses beyond PSYC 1100, for five psychology courses in all.

requirements.name: Philosophy Courses
requirements.description: Seven philosophy courses: two in the history of philosophy (usually PHIL 1125 and PHIL 1126, or DRST 0003 and DRST 0004); one logic course, PHIL 1115 suggested, preferably by the fall of junior year; two seminars, one of which may be in the Psychology department with DUS approval; and two intermediate or advanced courses on the intersection of philosophy and psychology, at least one of them a philosophy seminar, both approved by the DUS.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: A philosophy seminar taken with the extra work the department requires — it may be the intersection seminar among the seven philosophy courses — or a one- or two-term independent project (PHIL 4490, PHIL 4491). Add the seminar manually if you take that route.

MMES_BA.name: Modern Middle East Studies, B.A.
MMES_BA.description: Interdisciplinary major focusing on the modern Middle East, integrating culture, history, language, and society. Courses span the region's major languages and multiple academic disciplines.

requirements.name: Introductory Survey Courses
requirements.description: Two introductory survey courses on the Middle East focusing on the modern period. The DUS approves the courses that count, so add yours manually.

requirements.name: Regional Breadth
requirements.description: Two of the eight distribution courses must cover different regions or countries within the Middle East. Add yours manually.

requirements.name: Disciplinary Breadth
requirements.description: Two of the eight distribution courses must come from two different departments or programs. Add yours manually.

requirements.name: Pre-1750 Content
requirements.description: Two of the eight distribution courses must focus substantially on the period before 1750. Add yours manually.

requirements.name: Advanced Seminars
requirements.description: Two of the eight distribution courses must be advanced seminars. Add yours manually.

requirements.name: Middle East Language at L5
requirements.description: One course at the L5 level in a Middle Eastern language (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish). With DUS approval, up to two language courses below L5 may instead count toward the distribution requirements. Add yours manually.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: A senior essay using materials in a modern Middle Eastern language: one-term (MMES 491, listed in the catalog as MMES 4491) or two-term (MMES 493, listed as MMES 4492 and MMES 4493). Alternatively, majors may take an additional seminar and write the essay in that course, which you can add manually.

CPSC_MATH_BS.name: Computer Science and Mathematics, B.S.
CPSC_MATH_BS.description: The Computer Science and Mathematics major at Yale integrates foundational knowledge from both disciplines. The major requires 14 term courses (not including the senior project), split between 6 in Computer Science and 8 in Mathematics. Students complete a senior project or essay acceptable to both departments.

requirements.name: Introduction to Computer Science
requirements.description: CPSC 2010, one of the six Computer Science courses in the major.

requirements.name: Data Structures and Programming Techniques
requirements.description: CPSC 2230.

requirements.name: Systems Programming and Computer Organization
requirements.description: CPSC 3230.

requirements.name: Algorithms
requirements.description: Either CPSC 3650 or CPSC 3660. Only one of the two may count toward the major.

requirements.name: Additional CS
requirements.description: Two more Computer Science courses: one advanced course with significant mathematical content, and one further advanced course other than CPSC 4900. A course counts only if it carries a CPSC number; substitutions from other departments are not allowed.

requirements.name: Multivariable Calculus
requirements.description: MATH 1200. MATH 3020 may be substituted, but students without prior multivariable calculus must consult the Math DUS first, and MATH 3020 itself requires MATH 2250 and MATH 2550.

requirements.name: Linear Algebra
requirements.description: Either MATH 2250 or MATH 2260. MATH 2220 does not satisfy this requirement.

requirements.name: Discrete Mathematics
requirements.description: MATH 2440.

requirements.name: Additional Math
requirements.description: Five more Mathematics courses numbered 2250-4690, which rules out MATH 4700 and the senior seminars MATH 4800-4890. A course counts only if it carries a MATH number; graduate MATH courses 5000-5999 may count as electives, 6000 and above may not.

requirements.name: Senior Project or Essay
requirements.description: A project or essay on a topic acceptable to both departments, over and above the fourteen courses. Students typically enroll in CPSC 4900 or MATH 4750, and written permission from both DUSes is required before starting.

NELC_DEPTH_BA.name: Near Eastern Languages & Civilizations, B.A. (Depth Concentration)
NELC_DEPTH_BA.description: For students wishing to focus deeply on one or two Near Eastern languages and their associated civilizations.

requirements.name: Near Eastern Language
requirements.description: Six term courses in one or two Near Eastern languages (modern Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish; classical Arabic or Persian; Biblical Hebrew, Assyrian & Babylonian, Egyptian, Old Persian, Ottoman Turkish, Syriac, or Sumerian). Any approved course in the chosen language counts, so add yours manually.

requirements.name: NELC Foundations Course
requirements.description: One NELC Foundations course. The department publishes the approved list each year, so add yours manually.

requirements.name: NELC Electives
requirements.description: Four NELC electives chosen in consultation with the DUS. No more than two may come from other departments or programs, and at most two outside credits (transfer or study abroad) may count.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: One-semester senior project (NELC 4920) or yearlong senior project (NELC 4930). In rare cases, with prior written approval, an expanded upper-level seminar paper may substitute.

NELC_BREADTH_BA.name: Near Eastern Languages, Civilizations, and Culture, B.A. (Breadth Concentration)
NELC_BREADTH_BA.description: For students seeking broad coverage of Near Eastern languages, civilizations, and cultures across history. Must include electives on the ancient, medieval, and modern Near East.

requirements.name: Near Eastern Language
requirements.description: Four term courses in one or more Near Eastern languages (modern Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish; classical Arabic or Persian; Biblical Hebrew, Assyrian & Babylonian, Egyptian, Old Persian, Ottoman Turkish, Syriac, or Sumerian). Any approved course in those languages counts, so add yours manually.

requirements.name: NELC Foundations Courses
requirements.description: Two NELC Foundations courses. The department publishes the approved list each year, so add yours manually.

requirements.name: NELC Electives (with coverage)
requirements.description: Five NELC electives, including at least one on the ancient Near East, one on the medieval Near East, and one on the modern Middle East. No more than two may come from other departments or programs, and at most two outside credits (transfer or study abroad) may count.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: One-semester senior project (NELC 4920) or yearlong senior project (NELC 4930). In rare cases, with prior written approval, an expanded upper-level seminar paper may substitute.

PHYS_PHIL_BS.name: Physics and Philosophy, B.S.
PHYS_PHIL_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Physics and Philosophy

requirements.name: Math through Calc III
requirements.description: Mathematics through calculus at the level of MATH 1200.

requirements.name: Introductory Physics Sequence
requirements.description: Two courses: one complete lecture sequence, PHYS 1700 and 1710 or higher, so PHYS 1700 and 1710, or PHYS 1800 and 1810, or PHYS 2000 and 2010, or PHYS 2600 and 2610. Both halves must come from the same sequence, and each sequence has its own math corequisites.

requirements.name: Introductory Physics Lab
requirements.description: PHYS 2050L on its own, or the two-term sequence PHYS 1650L and PHYS 1660L (PHYS 1650L comes first). Each of these labs is worth half a credit.

requirements.name: Advanced Physics Lab
requirements.description: PHYS 2060L, worth half a credit. It is one of the eight required physics courses.

requirements.name: Math Methods for Physics
requirements.description: PHYS 4000 or an equivalent approved by the DUS. Counts as one of the seven advanced physics courses.

requirements.name: Quantum Mechanics
requirements.description: Either PHYS 4390 or PHYS 4400. Counts as one of the seven advanced physics courses.

requirements.name: Advanced PHYS Electives
requirements.description: Five further physics courses numbered 3000 or above, approved by the DUS. With PHYS 4000 and the quantum mechanics course these make up the seven advanced physics courses. One term of PHYS 4710 or 4720 may be used for one of the five. Physics courses must be taken for a letter grade.

requirements.name: Ancient Philosophy
requirements.description: PHIL 1125. Prospective majors should take at least two of the required philosophy courses by the end of sophomore year.

requirements.name: Modern Philosophy
requirements.description: PHIL 1126.

requirements.name: Philosophy/HSHM Electives
requirements.description: Four further courses in Philosophy or in History of Science, Medicine, and Public Health, which must include one logic course above the introductory level and one philosophy seminar chosen with the approval of the directors of undergraduate studies.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement (B.S. only)
requirements.description: PHYS 4710 and/or PHYS 4720. Only one term may count toward the eight required physics courses, so a student who takes both terms uses the second as one of the fifteen courses of the major.

PHYS_PHIL_BA.name: Physics and Philosophy, B.A.
PHYS_PHIL_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Physics and Philosophy

requirements.name: Senior Requirement (B.A. only)
requirements.description: PHIL 4490 or PHIL 4491 (the senior essay), or a philosophy seminar approved by both the Philosophy DUS and the seminar's instructor. Students in the Class of 2027 or 2028 who declared the major before fall 2026 may instead use PHIL 4480.

AMST.name: American Studies, B.A.
AMST.description: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies: fourteen approved term courses — four gateway courses, two junior seminars, five courses in an area of concentration, two AMST electives, and the senior requirement.

requirements.name: Cultural History/Cultural Studies
requirements.description: Two of the four gateway courses (AMST 1000-2999) must be in cultural history or cultural studies. One of the four gateway courses overall must carry the "Early Americas" attribute, and all four should be finished by the end of sophomore year, at the latest by the end of junior year. With DUS permission a First-Year Seminar may substitute for a gateway course.

requirements.name: American Literature Survey
requirements.description: One broad survey course in American literature, counting as one of the four gateway courses (AMST 1000-2999).

requirements.name: Preparation for Area of Concentration
requirements.description: One gateway course (AMST 1000-2999) preparing for the chosen area of concentration, selected in consultation with the DUS.

requirements.name: Junior Seminars
requirements.description: Two junior seminars (AMST 3000-3999) taken during the junior year, or one in the spring of sophomore year if planning to be abroad junior year. At least one must be in the area of concentration. Each requires critical essays on primary sources or a paper of fifteen to twenty pages.

requirements.name: Area of Concentration
requirements.description: Five courses from diverse disciplines in the area of concentration — national formations; the international United States; material cultures and built environments; politics and American communities; visual, audio, literary, and performance cultures; public humanities; or an independent concentration approved by the DUS. All five must be taken for a letter grade, one must treat a comparable topic from a non-U.S. perspective, and one may be a term of the two-term intensive senior project.

requirements.name: AMST Electives
requirements.description: Two electives chosen from the American Studies course offerings.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: One of: a senior seminar in the area of concentration (AMST 4000-4999, with a twenty to twenty-five page research paper); the one-term senior project AMST 4491 (thirty-page essay or equivalent); or, for the intensive major, the two-term project AMST 4493 and 4494 (sixty-page essay or equivalent), of which one term may count toward the area of concentration. A senior seminar is not a fixed course number, so record it with the manual option.

CSLI_BA.name: Computing and Linguistics, B.A.
CSLI_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in Computing and Linguistics

requirements.name: Statistics Prereq
requirements.description: Satisfied by S&DS 1000, 1230, 2200, or comparable experience (e.g., AP Statistics 5, with DUS approval).

requirements.name: Programming Prereq
requirements.description: Satisfied by any introductory programming course or comparable experience with DUS approval.

requirements.name: Linguistics Prereq
requirements.description: Any 1000-level LING course.

requirements.name: Discrete Mathematics Core
requirements.description: One proof-based discrete mathematics course: MATH 2440, LING 2249, or CPSC 2020.

requirements.name: Linear Algebra Core
requirements.description: One linear algebra course: MATH 2220 or MATH 2250.

requirements.name: Statistics Core
requirements.description: S&DS 2380, the statistics foundation for the B.A. degree.

requirements.name: Computation Core I
requirements.description: CPSC 2010, Introduction to Computer Science.

requirements.name: Computation Core II
requirements.description: CPSC 2230, Data Structures and Programming Techniques.

requirements.name: Linguistics Core Courses
requirements.description: Two of the three linguistics core courses: LING 2320 (phonology), LING 2530 (syntax), LING 2630 (semantics).

requirements.name: Advanced Linguistics Structure Course
requirements.description: One advanced course in linguistic structure: LING 3350, LING 3540, or LING 3640.

requirements.name: Advanced Natural Language Processing Course
requirements.description: One course in natural language processing: CPSC 4770 or LING 2270.

requirements.name: Advanced Course in Machine Learning
requirements.description: One course in machine learning: S&DS 2650, S&DS 3650, or CPSC 3810.

requirements.name: Elective
requirements.description: One elective in comp linguistics, NLP, ML, or related area (as approved by the DUS). See approved electives on the CSLI website.

requirements.name: Capstone Seminar and Senior Project
requirements.description: CSLI 490, the capstone seminar, in the fall of senior year. B.A. students complete a senior project as part of the seminar, either independently under a Yale faculty adviser or as part of a group effort of seminar participants.

CSLI_BS.name: Computing and Linguistics, B.S.
CSLI_BS.description: Bachelor of Science in Computing and Linguistics

requirements.name: Statistics Prereq
requirements.description: Prerequisite. Satisfied by S&DS 1000, 1230, 2200, or comparable experience (e.g., AP Statistics 5, with DUS approval).

requirements.name: Programming Prereq
requirements.description: Prerequisite. Satisfied by any introductory programming course or comparable experience with DUS approval.

requirements.name: Linguistics Prereq
requirements.description: Prerequisite. Any 1000-level LING course.

requirements.name: Discrete Mathematics Core
requirements.description: One proof-based discrete mathematics course: MATH 2440, LING 2249, or CPSC 2020.

requirements.name: Linear Algebra Core
requirements.description: One linear algebra course: MATH 2220 or MATH 2250.

requirements.name: Statistics Core Courses
requirements.description: Two courses in probability and statistical theory, on one of two routes: (1) S&DS 2400 or S&DS 2410, together with S&DS 2420; or (2) S&DS 2380 together with either S&DS 2300 or any S&DS course numbered 2420 or above.

requirements.name: Computation Core I
requirements.description: CPSC 2010, Introduction to Computer Science.

requirements.name: Computation Core II
requirements.description: CPSC 2230, Data Structures and Programming Techniques.

requirements.name: Linguistics Core Courses
requirements.description: All three linguistics core courses: LING 2320 (phonology), LING 2530 (syntax), and LING 2630 (semantics). The B.S. degree requires all three, unlike the B.A.

requirements.name: Advanced Linguistics Structure Course
requirements.description: One advanced course in linguistic structure: LING 3350, LING 3540, or LING 3640.

requirements.name: Advanced Natural Language Processing Course
requirements.description: One course in natural language processing: CPSC 4770 or LING 2270.

requirements.name: Advanced Course in Machine Learning
requirements.description: One course in machine learning: S&DS 2650, S&DS 3650, or CPSC 3810.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.description: Two electives in comp linguistics, NLP, ML, or related areas (as approved by the DUS). See approved electives on the CSLI website.

requirements.name: Capstone Seminar
requirements.description: CSLI 490, the capstone seminar, in the fall of senior year.

requirements.name: Additional Senior Project Course
requirements.description: One further term, normally in the spring, continuing the senior project begun in the capstone seminar. B.S. senior projects must involve independent research.

GMAN_BA.name: German Studies, B.A.
GMAN_BA.description: Bachelor of Arts in German Studies. Ten courses above the introductory sequence, including the senior essay.

requirements.name: Prerequisite
requirements.description: First- and second-year German, that is through GMAN 1400, or the equivalent by placement. The prerequisite is not one of the ten courses for the major.

requirements.name: 1500-level GMAN course
requirements.description: At least one GMAN course numbered in the 1500s.

requirements.name: 1600-level GMAN course
requirements.description: At least one GMAN course numbered in the 1600s (Group B, taught and read in German).

requirements.name: 1700-level GMAN course
requirements.description: At least one GMAN course numbered in the 1700s (Group B, taught and read in German).

requirements.name: Electives: Groups B & C (GMAN 1600+)
requirements.description: Six more GMAN courses numbered 1600 and above, from Groups B and C.

requirements.name: Senior Essay Tutorial
requirements.description: Senior essay tutorial, GMAN 4920, normally taken in the fall of the senior year.

GMAN_BA_INTENSIVE.name: German Studies, B.A. (Intensive)
GMAN_BA_INTENSIVE.description: Intensive version of German Studies major: replaces one advanced elective with a second term of the senior essay (GMAN 4930), for students seeking deeper research experience.

requirements.name: Senior Essay Tutorial

requirements.name: Senior Essay Second Term
requirements.description: GMAN 4930, the second term of the senior essay, in which the fifty- to sixty-page essay is completed.

MB&B_BA.name: Molecular Biophysics & Biochemistry, B.A.
MB&B_BA.description: Focuses on the molecular, chemical, and biophysical foundations of biology, with flexibility for students interested in the science-society interface. Suitable for students considering diverse careers in science, health, or related fields.

requirements.name: Introductory Biology
requirements.description: BIOL 1010 and BIOL 1020 (half credit each). Some concentrations also expect BIOL 1030 and 1040.

requirements.name: General Chemistry Lectures
requirements.description: Two terms of general chemistry: CHEM 1610 and CHEM 1650. The discontinued CHEM 1630/1670 sequence also counts.

requirements.name: General Chemistry Labs
requirements.description: CHEM 1340L and CHEM 1360L (half credit each, 1 credit in total).

requirements.name: Organic Chemistry Lecture
requirements.description: One term of organic chemistry: CHEM 2200 or CHEM 1740.

requirements.name: Organic Chemistry Lab
requirements.description: CHEM 2220L (half credit).

requirements.name: Calculus
requirements.description: Two terms of calculus: MATH 1120 followed by MATH 1150 or MATH 1160.

requirements.name: Biophysics Core
requirements.description: Three credits: one term of biophysical chemistry (MB&B 2750 or CHEM 3320) plus two terms of physics from one sequence, PHYS 1700 and 1710 or higher.

requirements.name: Biochemistry Core
requirements.description: MB&B 3000 and MB&B 3010 (no substitutions permitted), plus CHEM 1750 or another 2000-level chemistry course.

requirements.name: Science and Society Core
requirements.description: A half credit on where molecular biophysics and biochemistry meets human identity and society. MB&B 2680 is the recommended course; the listed alternatives are MB&B 1070, HSHM 2060, 4060, 4240, 4810, SOCY 1600, 1601, and 3760. You may petition for other substitutions.

requirements.name: Practical Skills
requirements.description: One credit of practical skills, either one full-credit course or two half-credit courses spread across two or three of the physics lab, biochemistry lab, and critical tools categories. At least a half credit must come from MB&B. Other 2000-level lab courses count with DUS approval.

requirements.name: MB&B Elective
requirements.description: One MB&B lecture or seminar course numbered 2000 or above, beyond the courses counted elsewhere in the major.

requirements.name: Senior Requirement
requirements.description: A one-credit senior essay: MB&B 4900 (literature project) or MB&B 4910 (essay drawing on laboratory research at Yale).

MB&B_BS.name: Molecular Biophysics & Biochemistry, B.S.
MB&B_BS.description: Provides rigorous training in the molecular basis of biology, preparing students for advanced study and careers in research, biotechnology, and medicine.
